those skilled in deliberative discussion understand this.
Therefore, if one wants to create squares and circles
and follows the compass and square,
then the achievements of all affairs will take shape.
And all things have compasses and squares;
those who deliberate and speak
consider and understand these.
The sage completely follows the compasses and squares of all things,
therefore it is said:
"Dare not be the first in the world."
Not daring to be the first in the world
means there is nothing one does not attend to,
no achievement is impossible,
and one's discussions will surely surpass the world.
If one desires not to hold a high office,
is that possible?
Holding a high office means being a leader in accomplishing things.
Therefore, it is said:
"Not daring to be the first in the world,
therefore one can be a leader in accomplishing things."
One who is kind to their children
dares not cut off their clothing and food;
one who is kind to themselves
dares not deviate from laws and standards;
one who is kind to squares and circles
dares not abandon the compass and square.
Therefore, when facing battle
and being kind to officers and soldiers,
one will defeat the enemy;
being kind to weapons and equipment,
the city will be strong and secure.
Therefore, it is said:
"Kindness,
in battle leads to victory,
in defense leads to security."
One who can preserve oneself
and completely follow the principles of all things
will surely have a natural endowment.
This natural endowment
is the generation of the mind,
therefore, the way of the world is completely generated by it.
If one uses kindness to protect it,
affairs will be perfectly safe
and every action will be appropriate,
then it is called a treasure.
Therefore, it is said:
"I have three treasures,
which I hold and treasure."
What the texts call the "great way," 〓#
is the correct way.
What is called the "appearance of lavishness,"
is the crooked way.
What is called "great path"
is beauty and splendor.
Beauty and splendor
are a part of the crooked way.
"The court is excessively clean"
means lawsuits are numerous.
When lawsuits are numerous,
fields are neglected;
when fields are neglected,
government granaries become empty;
when government granaries become empty,
the state becomes poor;
when the state is poor,
the customs of the people become extravagant and wasteful;
when the customs of the people become extravagant and wasteful,
the occupations of clothing and food cease;
when the occupations of clothing and food cease,
the people cannot help but engage in elaborate trickery;
engaging in elaborate trickery
means knowing how to adorn writing,
knowing how to adorn writing is called "wearing adorned writings."
When lawsuits are numerous,
and granaries are empty,
and people are used to extravagance,
then the injury to the state
is like piercing it with a sharp sword.
Therefore, it is said:
"Wearing a sharp sword."
Those who deliberately use their intelligence
to the point of harming the state,
their private families will surely be rich;
when private families are rich,
it is said:
"Having surplus wealth and goods."
If a state has such people,
then the foolish people cannot help but imitate them;
imitating them
leads to the birth of petty thieves.
From this perspective,
when great villains arise, petty thieves follow;
when great villains sing, petty thieves harmonize.
The yú (竽, a reed instrument)
is the leader of the five tones,
therefore, when the yú starts, the zhōng (鐘, bell) and sè (瑟, zither) all follow;
when the yú sings, all the music harmonizes.
Now, when great villains arise, the common people sing along;
when the common people sing along, the petty thieves will surely harmonize.
Therefore, "wearing adorned writings,
carrying sharp swords,
indulging in food and drink,
and having surplus wealth and goods
are what is called the thieves' yú."
Whether people are foolish or wise,
none do not have preferences and aversions.
Being tranquil and at peace,
none do not know the source of fortune and misfortune.
Being caught by likes and dislikes,
startled by excessive things,
then disorder arises.
The reason for this is
being drawn by external things
and disordered by cherished objects.
Being tranquil has the meaning of preferences and aversions,
being at peace knows the plans for fortune and misfortune.
But now, cherished objects change them,
external things draw them.
Being drawn and going along,
therefore it is called "jiào" (校, comparing, scrutinizing).
The most holy people are not like this:
once they establish their preferences and aversions,
even if they see things they like,
they cannot be drawn,
not being drawn is called "bù jiào" (不校, not scrutinizing).
Accordance with one's true feelings,
even if there are desirable things,
the spirit is not moved,
the spirit not being moved is called "not being pleased."
Those who are sons and grandsons,
embody this principle to protect the ancestral temple,
the ancestral temple not being destroyed
is called "the sacrifices not being cut off."
One's person takes accumulating essence as virtue,
the family takes resources and wealth as virtue,
the village, state, and the world all take the people as virtue.
Now, governing oneself
such that external things cannot disrupt one's spirit,
therefore it is said:
"Cultivate the person,
then one's virtue is genuine."
Genuine means
cautiously guarding it firmly.
Governing the family
such that useless things cannot affect one's plans,
then resources are abundant,
therefore it is said:
"Cultivate the family,
then one's virtue is surplus."
Governing the village
by practicing this principle,
then families with surpluses increase in number,
therefore it is said:
"Cultivate the village,
then one's virtue grows."
Governing the state
by practicing this principle,
then villages with virtue increase in number,
therefore it is said:
"Cultivate the state,
then one's virtue is abundant."
Governing the world
by practicing this principle,
then the lives of the people all receive its benefit,
therefore it is said:
"Cultivate the world,
then one's virtue is universal."
Those who cultivate themselves
use this to distinguish between the Junzi and the Xiaoren,
those who govern the village, state, and world,
each use this standard
to observe increase and decrease accordingly,
then nothing will be lost.
Therefore it is said:
"Use the self to observe the self,
use the family to observe the family,
use the village to observe the village,
use the state to observe the state,
use the world to observe the world.
How do I know the state of the world?
Through this."
When the world is governed,
there are no pressing calamities,
then it is called stillness,
urgent edicts are not used.
Therefore it is said:
"Turn back the galloping horses to manure the fields."
When the world is not governed,
attacks do not cease,
they defend each other for years without end,
lice and nits grow on the armor,
swallows and sparrows nest in the tents,
and the soldiers do not return.
Therefore it is said:
"Warhorses are born in the suburbs."
A Dí rén offered a plump fox and a
black leopard skin to Jìn Wén Gōng.
Wén Gōng received the guest's skin and sighed, saying:
"This is using the beauty of the skin to create its own crime."
Those who govern a state
take fame and reputation as a crime;
Xú Yǎn Wáng is an example of this.
Taking cities and lands as a crime;
Yú and Guó are examples of this.
Therefore it is said:
"No crime is greater than being desirable."
Zhì Bó combined the forces of Fàn and Zhōngháng
and attacked Zhào relentlessly,
Hán and Wèi rebelled against him,
the army was defeated at Jìnyáng,
he died east of Gāoliáng,
and eventually his territory was divided,
and his head was lacquered to be used as a chamber pot.
Therefore it is said:
"No misfortune is greater than not knowing contentment."
The ruler of Yú desired the carriage from Qūchǎn
and the jade from Chuíjí,
and did not listen to Gōng Zhīqí,
therefore his state was destroyed and he died.
Therefore it is said:
"No fault is more severe than wanting to gain."
A state takes survival as the norm;
becoming a Hegemon is just possible.
The person takes life as the norm;
wealth and status are just possible.
If one does not harm oneself with desire,
then the state will not be destroyed,
and the person will not die.
Therefore it is said:
"Knowing contentment is true contentment."
After Chǔ Zhuāng Wáng was victorious,
he hunted at Héyōng,
and upon returning, he rewarded Sūn Shū'áo.
Sūn Shū'áo requested land in the Hàn region,
a place with sand and rocks.
According to the laws of the state of Chǔ,
the land of ministers would be taken back after two generations,
but Sūn Shū'áo's land was the only exception.
This was because his state was not worth taking,
it was barren,
therefore sacrifices to him were not cut off for nine generations.
Therefore it is said:
"What is well established cannot be uprooted,
what is well embraced cannot be slipped,
descendants use this to continue their sacrifices
generation after generation without ceasing."
This refers to Sūn Shū'áo.
Control being in oneself is called weight;
not leaving one's position is called stillness.
Weight
enables the use of lightness,
stillness
enables the use of agitation.
Therefore it is said:
"Weight is the root of lightness,
stillness is the master of agitation."
Therefore it is said:
"The Junzi travels all day,
without leaving his baggage."
The state is
the baggage of the ruler.
Zhǔ Fù Shēng passed on his state,
this is leaving one's baggage;
therefore, although there was the pleasure of Dài and Yúnzhōng,
he was soon without Zhào.
Zhǔ Fù,
the ruler of ten thousand chariots,
took his body as lighter than the world.
Lacking authority is called lightness;
leaving one's position is called agitation;
therefore, he lived imprisoned and died.
Therefore it is said:
"Lightness leads to losing ministers,
agitation leads to losing the ruler."
This refers to Zhǔ Fù.
Heavy authority is the abyss of the ruler.
For one who rules,
authority is weighty among his ministers;
if lost, it cannot be regained.
Jiǎn Gōng lost it to Tián Chéng,
Jìn Gōng lost it to the Six Ministers,
and their states were destroyed and they died.
Therefore it is said:
"Fish cannot be separated from the deep abyss."
Rewards and punishments are the sharp weapons of the state.
If in the hands of the ruler
then they control the ministers;
if in the hands of the ministers
then they overcome the ruler.
When the ruler shows rewards,
the ministers diminish them to show their kindness;
when the ruler shows punishments,
the ministers increase them to show their power.
When the ruler shows rewards,
the ministers use his authority;
when the ruler shows punishments,
the ministers ride on his power.
Therefore it is said:
"The sharp weapons of the state
should not be shown to others."
The King of Yuè, Gōujiàn, became a vassal to the State of Wú,
and observed Wú's campaigns against Qí to exhaust Wú.
The Wú army had already defeated the Qí people at Àilíng,
displayed its strength between the Jiāng and Jì rivers,
and exerted its power at Huángchí.
Thus, it could be controlled at the Five Lakes.
Therefore it is said:
"If you wish to contract something,
you must first expand it;
if you wish to weaken something,
you must first strengthen it."
When Duke Xiàn of Jìn was about to attack Yú,
he presented Yú with precious jades and fine horses.
When Zhī Bó was about to attack Qiúyóu,
he presented Qiúyóu with grand chariots.
Therefore it is said:
"If you wish to take something,
you must first give it."
To initiate affairs from the imperceptible
and achieve great success in the world –
this is called subtle insight.
To be in a position of smallness and weakness, yet to humble and diminish oneself even further –
this is called the weak overcoming the strong.
Among things with form,
the great must arise from the small;
among things that endure,
the many must arise from the few.
Therefore it is said:
"The difficult tasks in the world must begin with the easy;
the great tasks in the world must begin with the subtle."
Therefore, those who wish to control things do so when they are subtle.
Thus it is said:
"Plan for the difficult when it is easy;
do the great when it is subtle."
A dike of a thousand zhàng collapses due to an ant's nest;
a house of a hundred chǐ burns due to a spark from a chimney crack.
Therefore it is said:
Bái Guī, when repairing dikes, stopped up their holes;
an elder, when being careful with fire, plastered over the cracks.
Thus, Bái Guī had no flood disaster,
and the elder had no fire calamity.
These are all examples of being careful with the easy
to avoid the difficult,
and respecting the subtle
to keep afar from the great.
Biǎn Què saw Marquis Huán of Cài,
and stood for a moment.
Biǎn Què said:
"Your Lordship has an illness in the interstitial skin,
if not treated, I fear it will deepen."
Marquis Huán said:
"I, the lonely one, have no illness."
When Biǎn Què left,
Marquis Huán said:
"Physicians like to treat the non-sick
to claim merit."
After ten days,
Biǎn Què saw him again and said:
"Your Lordship's illness is in the muscles and skin,
if not treated, it will deepen further."
Marquis Huán did not respond.
Biǎn Què left.
Marquis Huán was again displeased.
After ten days,
Biǎn Què saw him again and said:
"Your Lordship's illness is in the intestines and stomach,
if not treated, it will deepen further."
Marquis Huán again did not respond.
Biǎn Què left.
Marquis Huán was again displeased.
After ten days,
Biǎn Què looked at Marquis Huán and turned to run away.
Marquis Huán therefore sent someone to ask him.
Biǎn Què said:
"When the illness is in the interstitial skin,
it can be reached by hot compresses and moxibustion;
when it is in the muscles and skin,
it can be reached by acupuncture and stone needles;
when it is in the intestines and stomach,
it can be reached by fire-administered medicines;
but when it is in the bone marrow,
it belongs to the jurisdiction of Sīmìng,
there is nothing that can be done.
Now it is in the bone marrow,
therefore, I have no further request."
After five days,
Marquis Huán's body was in pain.
He sent someone to search for Biǎn Què,
but he had already fled to Qín.
Marquis Huán subsequently died.
Therefore, a good physician, in treating illness,
attacks it in the interstitial skin;
these are all cases of contending with the small.
Indeed, the blessings and misfortunes of affairs
also have their interstitial skin.
Therefore, the sage engages with them early.
In the past, when Prince Chóng'ěr of Jìn was in exile,
he passed through Zhèng,
but the Lord of Zhèng treated him disrespectfully.
Shū Zhān remonstrated, saying:
"This is a worthy prince;
if Your Lordship treats him generously,
you can accumulate virtue."
The Lord of Zhèng did not listen.
Shū Zhān again remonstrated, saying:
"If you do not treat him generously,
it would be better to kill him,
to prevent future trouble."
The Lord of Zhèng again did not listen.
When the prince returned to the state of Jìn,
he raised an army and attacked Zhèng,
severely defeating it,
and taking eight cities.
Duke Xiàn of Jìn used the jade of Chuíjī
to obtain passage through Yú to attack Guó.
Grand Master Gōng Zhīqí remonstrated, saying:
"This cannot be done.
If the lips are gone, the teeth will be cold.
Yú and Guó help each other,
not out of mutual virtue.
Today Jìn destroys Guó,
tomorrow Yú will surely follow in its destruction."
The Lord of Yú did not listen,
accepted the jade, and granted passage.
After Jìn had taken Guó,
it returned
and then destroyed Yú.
These two ministers
were both contending with the interstitial skin of affairs,
but the two lords did not use their advice.
Thus, Shū Zhān and Gōng Zhīqí
were also the Biǎn Què of Yú and Zhèng.
But the two lords did not listen,
so Zhèng was broken,
and Yú was destroyed.
Therefore it is said:
"What is stable is easy to hold;
what has not yet manifested is easy to plan for."
In the past, when Zhòu made ivory chopsticks,
Jī Zǐ sighed,
thinking
that ivory chopsticks would surely not be used with earthenware bowls,
but rather with rhinoceros horn and jade cups.
Ivory chopsticks and jade cups
would surely not be used for coarse vegetables and beans,
but rather for yak tails, elephant trunk, and leopard fetal meat.
Yak tails, elephant trunk, and leopard fetal meat
would surely not be eaten while wearing short coarse clothes
and dining under a thatched roof,
but rather in brocade robes of nine layers,
in vast halls and on high terraces.
I fear its end,
therefore I sigh at its beginning.
Five years later,
Zhòu made a meat forest,
set up the "Páoluò" torture,
climbed the hill of distiller's grains,
and overlooked the pool of wine.
Zhòu consequently perished.
Thus Jī Zǐ saw the ivory chopsticks
and knew the calamity of the world.
Therefore it is said:
"To see the small is to be clear-sighted."
Gōujiàn entered Wú as a vassal,
personally wielded weapons
and washed horses for the King of Wú,
and thus was able to kill Fūchā at Gūsū.
When King Wén was cursed at the palace gate,
his countenance did not change,
and King Wǔ captured Zhòu at Mùyě.
Therefore it is said:
"To maintain pliancy is to be strong."
When the King of Yuè achieved hegemony,
he was not troubled by his officials.
When King Wǔ ruled, he was not troubled by censure.
Therefore, it is said:
"The Sage is not troubled
because he is not troubled;
therefore, he has no troubles."
A rustic from Sòng obtained a piece of raw jade
and presented it to Zǐhǎn.
Zǐhǎn did not accept it.
The rustic said:
"This is a treasure,
suitable for a Jūnzǐ,
not suitable for use by a commoner."
Zǐhǎn said:
"You consider jade a treasure,
but I consider not accepting your jade a treasure."
Thus, the rustic desired jade,
but Zǐhǎn did not desire jade.
Therefore, it is said:
"Desire non-desire,
and do not value rare goods."
Wáng Shòu was walking, carrying books,
when he met Xú Féng on the road in Zhōu.
Xú Féng said:
"Matters
are for action;
actions arise from timeliness;
the wise have no fixed actions.
Books
are words;
words arise from understanding;
the wise do not hoard books.
Why do you alone carry them as you walk?"
Thereupon, Wáng Shòu burned his books and danced.
Therefore, the wise do not teach through discourse,
and the intelligent do not store books in chests.
This is what the world errs in,
but Wáng Shòu rectified it;
this is learning not to learn.
Therefore, it is said:
"Learning not to learn
is to return to that which the multitude has overlooked."
Indeed, things have a constant nature;
one should guide them by taking advantage of it.
By following the nature of things,
therefore, in stillness one establishes virtue,
and in activity one accords with the Dào.
There was a man from Sòng who made mulberry leaves out of ivory for his ruler.
It took him three years to complete.
The thick and thin veins and stems,
the fine hairs and intricate luster,
were so perfect that when mixed among real mulberry leaves,
they could not be distinguished.
This man thereupon received an emolument for his achievement in the state of Sòng.
Lièzǐ heard of this and said:
"If Heaven and Earth took three years to make one leaf,
then things with leaves would be few indeed."
Therefore, not relying on the resources of Heaven and Earth
and bearing the burden of one person,
not following the laws of principle
and learning the wisdom of one person—
these are all actions like making one leaf.
Thus, crops cultivated in winter,
Hòujì could not make them prosper;
a great harvest in a bountiful year,
even Zāng Huò could not find fault with.
If relying on one person's strength,
then Hòujì would be insufficient;
but if following nature,
then even Zāng Huò would have abundance.
"Rely on the spontaneity of all things
and dare not act (artificially)."
The orifices
are the doors and windows of spiritual insight.
If ears and eyes are exhausted by sounds and sights,
and the spirit is exhausted by external appearances,
then the interior has no master.
If the interior has no master,
then even if calamity and fortune are like hills and mountains,
there is no way to recognize them.
Therefore, it is said:
"Without going out the door,
one can know the world;
without peeking through the window,
one can know the Way of Heaven."
This speaks of spiritual insight not departing from its essence.
Lord Xiāng of Zhào learned chariot driving from Prince Yú Qí.
Soon after, he raced against Yú Qí.
He changed horses three times and was behind three times.
Lord Xiāng said:
"Has your teaching me to drive not fully conveyed the technique?"
He replied:
"The technique is complete,
but your application of it is flawed.
What is valued in chariot driving is that
the horse's body is at ease with the chariot,
and the driver's mind is in harmony with the horse.
Only then can one advance swiftly and reach far.
Now, when you are behind, you want to catch up with me, your minister;
when you are ahead, you fear I will catch up with you.
Indeed, in leading the way and striving for distance,
one is either ahead or behind.
But your mind, whether ahead or behind, is entirely focused on me, your minister.
How, then, can you harmonize with the horse?
This is why you are behind."
Bái Gōngshèng was contemplating rebellion.
After court was dismissed,
he inverted his staff and with its sharp end pierced his chin.
Blood flowed to the ground, yet he did not notice.
A man from Zhèng heard of it and said:
"If he forgets his own chin,
what else will he not forget?"
Therefore, it is said:
"The further one extends one's reach,
the less one's wisdom becomes."
This means that when wisdom encompasses distant things,
then what is neglected is close by.
Therefore, the Sage has no fixed actions.
Being able to encompass all wisdom,
it is said:
"He knows without acting."
Being able to encompass all sight,
it is said:
"He sees clearly without looking."
He undertakes affairs according to the times,
establishes achievements by relying on resources,
uses the abilities of all things
and obtains the greatest advantage from them.
Therefore, it is said:
"He achieves without acting."
King Zhuāng of Chǔ governed for three years,
no decrees were issued,
and no policies were enacted.
The Right Sīmǎ attended the King's seat
and spoke to the King in veiled terms, saying:
"There is a bird perched on a mound in the south.
For three years it has not flapped its wings,
neither flying nor singing,
silently without a sound.
What is this bird called?"
The King said:
"For three years it has not flapped its wings—
it intends to grow its wings.
Not flying, not singing—
it intends to observe the people's ways.
Although it has not flown,
when it flies, it will surely soar to the sky.
Although it has not sung,
when it sings, it will surely astonish people.
You may stop now;
I, the unworthy one, understand it."
After half a year,
he then personally attended to government.
Ten people were dismissed,
nine were appointed,
five great ministers were executed,
and six reclusive scholars were promoted.
Consequently, the state was greatly governed.
He raised an army and punished Qí,
defeating them at Xúzhōu.
He defeated Jìn at Hé Yōng,
assembled the feudal lords at Sòng,
and thus dominated the world.
King Zhuāng did not, for minor harm, compromise what was good,
therefore he gained a great reputation.
He did not reveal himself too early,
therefore he achieved great accomplishments.
Therefore, it is said:
"Great vessels are completed late;
the greatest sound is rare to hear."
Chǔ Zhuāng Wáng wanted to attack Yuè.
Dù Zǐ advised,
"What is the reason, O King, for attacking Yuè?"
He said,
"Their government is chaotic and their army is weak."
Dù Zǐ said,
"Your servant is foolishly worried about your
wisdom. It is like an eye,
able to see hundreds of steps away,
but unable to see its own eyelashes.
Your Majesty's army has repeatedly been defeated by Qín and Jìn,
losing hundreds of *lǐ* of territory.
This is the weakness of the army.
Zhuāng Xīqiāo becomes a bandit within the borders
and the officials cannot stop him.
This is the chaos of the government.
Your Majesty's weakness and chaos
are no less than those of Yuè.
Yet you want to attack Yuè?
This is wisdom like the eye."
The King then stopped.
Therefore, the difficulty of knowing
lies not in seeing others,
but in seeing oneself.
Therefore, it is said,
"Seeing oneself is called clarity."
Zǐ Xià went to see Zēng Zǐ.
Zēng Zǐ said,
"Why are you so fat?"
He replied,
"I won a battle,
therefore I am fat."
Zēng Zǐ said,
"What do you mean?"
Zǐ Xià said,
"When I enter and see the righteousness of the former kings,
I am honored by it.
When I go out and see the pleasures of wealth and nobility,
I am also honored by them.
These two battle in my chest,
and I do not know who will win,
therefore I am thin.
Now the righteousness of the former kings has won,
therefore I am fat."
Therefore, the difficulty of ambition
lies not in overcoming others,
but in overcoming oneself.
Therefore, it is said,
"Overcoming oneself is called strength."
The Zhōu had a jade tablet.
Zhòu ordered Jiāo Gé to obtain it,
but Wén Wáng did not give it.
Fèi Zhòng came to ask for it,
and he gave it to him.
This means Jiāo Gé was virtuous
and Fèi Zhòng was without principle.
Zhōu hated that the virtuous would gain their ambitions,
therefore he gave it to Fèi Zhòng.
Wén Wáng raised Tài Gōng from the banks of the Wèi River
to honor him;
and giving the jade tablet to Fèi Zhòng
was to love him.
Therefore, it is said,
"Not valuing one's teacher,
not cherishing one's resources,
although knowing, is greatly confused,
this is called essential mystery."
Tāng attacked Jié,
but feared that the world would say he was greedy,
so he abdicated the throne to Wù Guāng.
Fearing that Wù Guāng would accept it,
he sent someone to persuade Wù Guāng, saying,
"Tāng killed the ruler and wants to pass on a bad reputation to you,
so he abdicated the throne to you."
Wù Guāng then threw himself into the river.
Qín Wǔ Wáng ordered Gān Mào to choose what he wanted to be
between a stableman and an executive official.
Mèng Mǎo said,
"You are better off being a stableman.
What you are good at
is being employed.
Even if you are a stableman,
the king will still employ you as a public servant.
If you wear the seal of a stableman and act as an executive official,
that is holding concurrent offices."
Zǐ Yǔ saw Kǒng Zǐ at the place of the Shāng Grand Tutor.
Kǒng Zǐ left,
Zǐ Yǔ entered,
and inquired about the guest.
The Grand Tutor said,
"Once I had seen Kǒng Zǐ,
I regarded you as no more than a tiny flea.
I will now introduce him to the ruler."
Zǐ Yǔ, fearing that Kǒng Zǐ would be valued more than him by the ruler,
then said to the Grand Tutor,
"Once the ruler has seen Kǒng Zǐ,
he will also regard you as no more than a flea."
The Grand Tutor then did not introduce him again.
Wèi Huì Wáng formed the alliance of Jiùlǐ,
intending to be re-established by the Son of Heaven.
Péng Xǐ said to the ruler of Zhèng,
"Do not listen to him.
Large states hate having a Son of Heaven,
small states benefit from it.
If you and the large states do not listen,
how can Wèi establish him with the small states?"
The Jìn people attacked Xíng,
and Qí Huán Gōng was about to save it.
Bào Shū said,
"It is too early.
If Xíng does not perish,
Jìn will not be exhausted;
if Jìn is not exhausted,
Qí will not be respected.
Moreover, the merit of holding up what is in danger
is not as great as the virtue of preserving what is lost.
It would be better for you to save them late, after exhausting Jìn.
Qí will truly benefit.
Wait for Xíng to perish and then restore it,
and its name and reality will be beautiful."
Huán Gōng then did not save it.
Wǔ Zixū fled,
and a border guard caught him.
Wǔ Zixū said,
"The reason my lord is searching for me
is that I have a beautiful pearl.
Now I have already lost it.
I will say that
you took it and swallowed it."
The guard then released him.
Qìng Fēng caused chaos in Qí and wanted to flee to Yuè.
His clansmen said,
"Jìn is close,
why not go to Jìn?"
Qìng Fēng said,
"Yuè is far away,
which is advantageous for avoiding difficulty."
His clansmen said,
"If you change your heart,
living in Jìn would be acceptable;
if you do not change your heart,
even if Yuè is far away,
how can you be secure?"
Zhì Bó demanded territory from Wèi Xuānzǐ,
but Wèi Xuānzǐ did not give it to him.
Rèn Zhāng said,
"Why not give it to him?"
Xuānzǐ said,
"He is asking for territory for no reason,
therefore I am not giving it to him."
Rèn Zhāng said,
"Demanding territory for no reason,
neighboring countries will certainly fear.
If he is heavily desiring and insatiable,
the world will certainly be afraid.
If you give him the territory,
Zhì Bó will certainly become arrogant and underestimate his enemies,
and the neighboring states will certainly fear and become close to each other.
If you use an army that is close to each other to wait for a country that underestimates its enemies,
then Zhì Bó's life will not be long.
The *Zhōu Shū* says:
'If you want to ruin him,
you must first assist him;
if you want to take from him,
you must first give to him.'
You would be better off giving it to him to make Zhì Bó arrogant.
Moreover, why do you release the world to plot against the Zhì clan,
and only use our country as a pawn for the Zhì clan?"
The ruler said,
"Good."
He then gave him a city of ten thousand households.
Zhì Bó was very pleased
and then demanded territory from Zhào.
did not give it;
therefore besieged Jìnyáng 晉陽.
With Hán 韓 and Wèi 魏 rebelling from the outside,
and the Zhào 趙 clan responding from within,
the Zhì 智 clan perished.
Duke Kāng of Qín 秦康公 built a terrace for three years.
The Jīng 荊 people raised troops,
intending to use them to attack Qí 齊.
Rèn Wàng 任妄 said:
"Famine summons soldiers,
disease summons soldiers,
toil summons soldiers,
chaos summons soldiers.
Your lord has built a terrace for three years,
and now the Jīng 荊 people have raised troops and are about to attack Qí 齊.
I fear that their attack on Qí 齊 is a feint,
and their real intention is to attack Qín 秦,
it would be better to prepare for it."
He garrisoned the eastern border,
and the Jīng 荊 people ceased their advance.
Qí 齊 attacked Sòng 宋,
and Sòng 宋 sent Zāngsūn Zǐnán 臧孫子南 to seek help from Jīng 荊.
Jīng 荊 was greatly pleased,
promised to help,
and strongly encouraged them.
Zāngsūn Zǐ 臧孫子 was worried and returned.
His driver said:
"Having sought help and received it,
now you have a worried expression,
why is that?"
Zāngsūn Zǐ 臧孫子 said:
"Sòng 宋 is small and Qí 齊 is large.
To rescue small Sòng 宋 and offend large Qí 齊,
this is what people worry about;
yet the King of Jīng 荊 is pleased,
he must be relying on my steadfastness.
If I am steadfast and Qí 齊 is exhausted,
that is what Jīng 荊 benefits from."
Zāngsūn Zǐ 臧孫子 then returned.
The people of Qí 齊 seized five cities from Sòng 宋,
but the rescue from Jīng 荊 did not arrive.
Marquis Wén of Wèi 魏文侯 borrowed a road from Zhào 趙
in order to attack Zhōngshān 中山,
and Marquis Sù of Zhào 趙肅侯 was about to refuse.
Zhào Kè 趙刻 said:
"You are mistaken.
If Wèi 魏 attacks Zhōngshān 中山 and cannot take it,
then Wèi 魏 will certainly be exhausted.
If it is exhausted then Wèi 魏 will be weakened,
and if Wèi 魏 is weakened then Zhào 趙 will be strengthened.
If Wèi 魏 seizes Zhōngshān 中山,
it will certainly not be able to bypass Zhào 趙 and possess Zhōngshān 中山.
In this use of troops,
Wèi 魏 is the one expending effort;
but the one who gains territory
is Zhào 趙.
You must allow it.
Allow it while expressing great joy,
they will know that you benefit from it,
and will certainly cease their advance.
You would be better off lending them the road,
showing them that it is unavoidable."
Chīyí Zǐpí 鴟夷子皮 served Tián Chéngzǐ 田成子.
Tián Chéngzǐ 田成子 left Qí 齊,
fled to Yān 燕,
and Chīyí Zǐpí 鴟夷子皮 carried his baggage and followed him.
Reaching Wàng 望 village,
Zǐpí 子皮 said:
"Have you not heard of the snakes in the dried-up marsh?
When the marsh dried up,
the snakes were about to move.
A small snake said to a large snake:
'If you walk and I follow you,
people will think that it is just a snake walking,
and will certainly kill you.
It would be better for us to bite each other and you carry me as we walk,
and people will think of us as divine rulers.'
So they bit each other and he carried him
across the public road.
People all avoided them,
saying:
'It is a divine ruler!'
Now you are beautiful and I am ugly.
To regard you as my honored guest
is suitable for the ruler of a thousand chariots;
to regard you as my messenger
is suitable for a minister of ten thousand chariots.
You would be better off being my attendant."
Tián Chéngzǐ 田成子 then carried his baggage and followed him.
Reaching an inn,
the innkeeper treated him with great respect,
and offered wine and meat.
A man from Wēn 溫 went to Zhōu 周,
but Zhōu 周 did not admit guests.
He was asked:
"Are you a guest?"
He replied:
"A host."
They asked the people in the lane, but they did not know him,
so the officials imprisoned him.
The ruler sent someone to ask him:
"You are not a man of Zhōu 周,
and you claim not to be a guest,
why is that?"
He replied:
"When I was young I recited the *Shī* 《詩》, which says:
'Under all of vast heaven,
there is no land that is not the king's;
to the very borders of the soil,
there are none who are not the king's servants.'
Now you are
the Son of Heaven,
then I am a servant of the Son of Heaven.
How can one be a servant of a person
and also be their guest?
Therefore I say:
a host."
The ruler ordered him to be released.
King Xuān of Hán 韓宣王 said to Jiū Liú 樛留:
"I wish to employ both Gōngzhòng 公仲 and Gōngshū 公叔,
is that permissible?"
He replied:
"It is not permissible.
Jìn 晉 employed six ministers
and the country was divided;
Duke Jiǎn 簡公 employed both Tián Chéng 田成 and Kàn Zhǐ 闞止
and Duke Jiǎn 簡公 was killed;
Wèi 魏 employed both Xī Shǒu 犀首 and Zhāng Yí 張儀,
and the territory outside the West River was lost.
Now if you employ both of them,
the stronger will build up their faction,
and the weaker will borrow external power.
If there are ministers who build up internal factions to overawe the ruler,
and those who make external alliances to carve up territory,
then your kingdom will be in danger."
Shào Jì 紹績, being drunk, slept and lost his fur coat.
The ruler of Sòng 宋 said:
"Is drunkenness sufficient to lose a fur coat?"
He replied:
"Jié 桀 lost the world through drunkenness,
and the *Kāng Gào* 《康誥》 says
'do not be addicted to wine,'
'addicted to wine' means habitual drinking.
Habitual drinking
causes the Son of Heaven to lose the world,
and the common man to lose his life."
Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 and Xí Péng 隰朋 followed Duke Huán 桓公
to attack Gúzhú 孤竹,
going in spring and returning in winter,
becoming lost and losing their way.
Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 said:
"The wisdom of an old horse can be used."
So they released an old horse and followed it,
and thus found their way.
Traveling in the mountains without water,
Xí Péng 隰朋 said:
"Ants live on the sunny side of the mountain in winter,
and on the shady side of the mountain in summer.
Where the ant-heap is one inch deep, water is eight feet deep."
So they dug the ground,
and thus found water.
With the wisdom of Guǎn Zhòng 管仲
and the intelligence of Xí Péng 隰朋,
when they came to something they did not know,
they did not hesitate to learn from an old horse or ants.
Now people do not know how to use their foolish minds
to learn from the wisdom of sages,
is that not excessive?
Someone presented a medicine of immortality to the King of Jīng 荊,
and the gatekeeper took it in to present it.
A palace guard asked:
"Can it be eaten?"
He said:
"It can."
So he seized it and ate it.
The king was furious,
and ordered the palace guard to be killed.
The archer in the middle position had someone speak to the king, saying:
“Your servant asked the gatekeeper,
who said, ‘It is edible,’
so your servant ate it.
Therefore, your servant is without guilt,
and the fault lies with the gatekeeper.
Moreover, a guest presented a drug of immortality.
Your servant ate it, but the king will kill your servant.
This is a drug of death!
This is the guest deceiving the king!
To kill a guiltless minister,
and to make clear that others deceive the king,
it is better to release your servant.”
The king then did not kill him.
Tián Sì deceived the ruler of Zōu.
The ruler of Zōu was about to send someone to kill him.
Tián Sì was afraid
and told Huìzi.
Huìzi saw the ruler of Zōu and said:
“Now, if someone sees the ruler,
and winks one eye at him,
what would you think?”
The ruler said:
“I would certainly kill him.”
Huìzi said:
“A blind man,
both eyes wink.
Why doesn’t the ruler kill him?”
The ruler said:
“He cannot help but wink.”
Huìzi said:
“Tián Sì was disrespectful to the Marquis of Qí in the east,
and deceived the King of Jīng in the south.
Sì's deceiving people
is like a blind man.
Why does the ruler resent him?”
The ruler of Zōu then did not kill him.
Duke Mù of Lǔ had all of his sons
serve as officials either in Jìn
or in Jīng.
Lí Chú said:
“To borrow someone from Yuè to save a drowning child
even though the people of Yuè are good swimmers,
the child will certainly not live.
To put out a fire by fetching water from the sea,
even though the seawater is plentiful,
the fire will certainly not be extinguished,
distant water cannot save a nearby fire.
Now, although Jìn and Jīng are strong,
Qí is nearby.
Does Lǔ worry that they will not be saved?”
Yán Suì did not get along with the ruler of Zhōu,
and worried about it.
Féng Jū said:
“Yán Suì is the prime minister,
and Hán Kuí is favored by the ruler.
It would be better to commit an assault against Hán Kuí,
then the ruler will certainly think it was done by the Yán family.”
Zhāng Qiàn was the prime minister of Hán,
and was sick and about to die.
Gōngchéng Wúzheng brought thirty pieces of gold
and inquired about his illness.
After one day,
the ruler asked Zhāng Qiàn, saying:
“If you die,
whom shall I have replace you?”
He replied:
“Wúzheng values the law and fears his superior.
However,
he is not as good as Gōngzǐ Shíwǒ in winning the people.”
Zhāng Qiàn died,
and Gōngchéng Wúzheng consequently became prime minister.
Yuè Yáng, serving as a general of Wèi, attacked Zhōngshān.
His son was in Zhōngshān.
The ruler of Zhōngshān boiled his son
and sent him the soup.
Yuè Yáng sat under the tent and sipped it,
finishing one cup.
Marquis Wén said to Dǔ Shī Zàn:
“Yuè Yáng ate the flesh of his son because of me.”
He replied:
“He ate his own son,
who else would he not eat?”
Yuè Yáng withdrew from Zhōngshān.
Marquis Wén rewarded his accomplishment but suspected his heart.
Mèng Sūn hunted and obtained a fawn,
and had Qín Xībā hold it and return home.
Its mother followed it and cried.
Qín Xībā could not bear it and gave it to her.
Mèng Sūn returned
and when he arrived, he asked for the fawn.
He replied:
“I could not bear it and gave it to its mother.”
Mèng Sūn was greatly angered
and drove him away.
After three months,
he summoned him again to be the tutor of his son.
His charioteer said:
“Formerly, you were going to punish him,
now you summon him to be the tutor of your son.
Why is that?”
Mèng Sūn said:
“If he could not bear to harm the fawn,
how much more will he not bear to harm my son?”
Therefore, it is said:
“Skillful deceit is not as good as clumsy sincerity.”
Yuè Yáng was doubted because of his accomplishment.
Qín Xībā was trusted all the more because of his offense.
Zēng Cóngzi was skilled in appraising swords.
The ruler of Wèi resented the king of Wú.
Zēng Cóngzi said:
“The king of Wú likes swords.
Your servant is a sword appraiser.
Let me appraise swords for the king of Wú,
draw one and show it to him,
and then take the opportunity to assassinate him for you.”
The ruler of Wèi said:
“Your doing this
is not based on righteousness,
but for profit.
Wú is strong and wealthy,
Wèi is weak and poor.
You will certainly go there.
I fear that you will be used by the king of Wú against me.”
He then drove him away.
Zhòu used ivory chopsticks and Jīzi sighed,
thinking that ivory chopsticks
would certainly not be used to hold soup in earthenware pots,
but would certainly be in cups of rhinoceros horn and jade;
with jade cups and ivory chopsticks,
he would certainly not hold beans and greens,
but would certainly have the embryos of yaks, elephants, and leopards.
With embryos of yaks, elephants, and leopards,
he would certainly not wear short hemp garments
and live under a thatched roof,
but would certainly wear brocade robes in nine layers
and live in high platforms and spacious rooms.
Seeking these things in this way,
then the world would not be enough.
The sage sees the subtle and knows the sprouting,
sees the beginning and knows the end.
Therefore, seeing ivory chopsticks, he sighed,
knowing that the world would not be enough.
After the Duke of Zhōu, Dàn, had defeated Yīn,
he was about to attack Shānggài.
Xīn Gōngjiǎ said:
“The large is difficult to attack,
the small is easy to subdue.
It would be better to subdue the many small to threaten the large.”
Then he attacked the Nine Barbarians and Shānggài was subdued.
Zhòu engaged in drinking that lasted all night,
reveling to the point of losing track of the days.
He asked those around him,
but none of them knew.
Then he sent someone to ask Jīzi.
Jīzi said to his followers:
“Being the ruler of all under Heaven,
if the entire country loses track of the days,
then all under Heaven is in danger.
If the entire country does not know,
and I alone know,
then I am in danger.”
He excused himself by saying he was drunk and did not know.
A man of Lǔ was skilled at weaving straw sandals,
and his wife was skilled at weaving fine silk,
and they wanted to move to Yuè.
Someone said to them:
“You will certainly be impoverished.”
The man of Lǔ said:
“Why?”
He said:
“Shoes are made to be worn,
yet the Yuè people go barefoot;
plain silk is for making caps,
yet the Yuè people wear their hair loose.
Using your strengths
in a country where they are not needed,
and hoping to have endless success,
is that possible?”
Chén Zhěn was favored by the King of Wèi.
Huìzi said:
“You must treat those around the king well.
The yáng tree,
if planted sideways, will live;
if planted upside down, it will live;
if broken and planted, it will still live.
However, if ten people plant it
and one person pulls it up,
then no yáng tree will live.
Even with ten people
planting an easily grown thing,
they cannot overcome one person.
Why is that?
It is difficult to plant
but easy to remove.
Although you are skilled at establishing yourself with the king,
if many wish to remove you,
you will surely be in danger.”
Jìsūn of Lǔ had just murdered his ruler,
and Wú Qǐ went to serve him.
Someone said to Qǐ:
“A dead man,
when first dead, bleeds;
after bleeding, the blood stops;
after the blood stops, he turns to ash;
after ash, he becomes earth.
When he is earth,
there is nothing that can be done.
Now Jìsūn has only just begun to bleed;
perhaps the future is not yet certain.”
Wú Qǐ therefore left to go to Jìn.
Xí Sīmí saw Tián Chéngzǐ,
and Tián Chéngzǐ took him up to a terrace to look around.
Three sides were clear,
but looking south,
the trees of the Xí family blocked the view.
Tián Chéngzǐ did not say anything.
Xízi returned home
and had people chop down the trees.
After several blows with the axe,
Xízi stopped them.
His steward said:
“Why this sudden change?”
Xízi said:
“There is an ancient saying:
‘Knowing the fish in the deep is ominous.’
Tiánzi is planning something big,
and if I show him I know too much,
I will be in danger.
Not cutting down the trees
is not a crime;
knowing what others do not say,
that is a great crime.”
So he did not cut them down.
Yángzi was staying at an inn east of Sòng.
There were two concubines,
the ugly one was valued,
the beautiful one was cheap.
Yángzi asked the reason.
The innkeeper replied:
“The beautiful one assumes her own beauty,
I do not recognize her beauty;
the ugly one assumes her own ugliness,
I do not recognize her ugliness.”
Yángzi said to his disciples:
“Practice virtue
and abandon the thought of being virtuous,
and where can you go that you will not be admired?”
A man of Wèi married off his daughter and taught her:
“Be sure to secretly accumulate possessions.
For a woman to marry out is normal;
[to establish permanent residence with her husband] is fortunate.”
His daughter therefore secretly accumulated possessions,
and her mother-in-law, thinking she was too greedy, sent her away.
The possessions that his daughter brought back
were double what she had taken with her in marriage.
Her father did not blame himself for wrongly teaching his daughter,
but congratulated himself on becoming richer.
The way officials behave in their positions today
is all of this kind.
Lǔ Dān made three proposals to the ruler of Zhōngshān
but was not accepted, so he distributed fifty gold pieces to those around the ruler.
He visited again,
and before he spoke,
the ruler gave him food.
Lǔ Dān left,
and without returning to his lodgings,
he departed from Zhōngshān.
His driver said:
“On the contrary, when we visited, he began to treat me well.
Why did you leave him?”
Lǔ Dān said:
“If he praises me based on others' words,
he will surely condemn me based on others' words.”
Before he had left the border,
a young nobleman slandered him, saying:
“He came from Zhào to spy on Zhōngshān.”
The ruler therefore sought him out and punished him.
Tián Bódǐng favored scholars and preserved his ruler;
Bái Gōng favored scholars and caused chaos in Jīng.
Their favoring of scholars was the same;
what they did with it was different.
Gōngsūn Yǒu cut off his own feet to honor Bǎilǐ;
Shù Diāo castrated himself to flatter Duke Huán.
Their self-mutilation was the same;
what they did through their self-mutilation was different.
Huìzi said:
"A madman runs east,
and the one chasing him also runs east.
Their running east is the same;
what they do by running east is different.
Therefore, it is said:
'One must carefully observe those who do the same thing.'"
Bólè taught two people how to identify a kicking horse,
and together they went to the stables of Jiǎnzǐ to observe the horses.
One person pointed out a kicking horse.
The other person followed behind and stroked it,
stroking its rump three times, but the horse did not kick.
This person thought he had lost the ability to identify them.
The other person said:
“You have not lost the ability to identify them.
The reason this is a horse that does not kick
is because it has a sprained shoulder and swollen knees.
A kicking horse
lifts its rear and puts weight on its front,
but swollen knees cannot bear the weight,
so the rear cannot lift.
You are skilled at identifying kicking horses
but unskilled at recognizing swollen knees.”
Affairs have a certain destination to which they must return,
and not to take responsibility when there are swollen knees is something
only the wise know.
Huìzi said:
"Put a monkey in a cage,
and it is the same as a pig."
Therefore, when the situation is unfavorable,
it is not the time to show off one's abilities.
The general of Wèi, Wénzi, visited Zēngzi.
Zēngzi did not rise to greet him but gestured for him to sit on the mat,
straightening himself in the corner of the room.
Wénzi said to his driver:
"Zēngzi
is a foolish man!
If he thinks I am a gentleman,
how can a gentleman not be respected?
If he thinks I am a tyrant,
how can a tyrant be insulted?
That Zēngzi is not punished
is fate."
There is a bird with a heavy head and bent tail,
when it wants to drink from the river,
it will surely fall over.
Therefore, it holds its feathers in its mouth to drink.
For people, if there is something insufficient for drinking,
one must seek its feathers.
The *zhān* sturgeon resembles a snake,
and the silkworm resembles a caterpillar.
People, seeing a snake,
are terrified;
seeing a caterpillar,
their hair stands on end.
Fishermen hold the *zhān* sturgeon,
and women gather silkworms.
Where profit lies,
all become Bēn or Zhū.
Bólè teaches his hated ones how to recognize a thousand-*lǐ* horse,
but teaches his loved ones how to recognize a worthless horse.
A thousand-*lǐ* horse appears only once in a while,
and the profit from it is slow in coming;
a worthless horse is sold daily,
and the profit from it is quick.
This is what the *Zhōu Shū* calls
"When inferiors speak and superiors act,
it is delusion."
Huán Hè said:
"In the art of carving,
nothing is better than a large nose,
and small eyes.
A large nose can be made smaller,
but a small one cannot be made larger;
small eyes can be made larger,
but large ones cannot be made smaller."
Conducting affairs is also like this:
if you do things in a way that allows for reversal later,
then affairs will rarely fail.
Chóng Hóu and Èlái knew that they would not escape Zhòu's punishment,
but they did not see Wǔ Wáng's extermination of him.
Bǐgān and Zǐxū knew that their ruler was doomed,
but they did not know of their own deaths.
Therefore it is said:
"Chóng Hóu and Èlái knew the heart but not the matter;
Bǐgān and Zǐxū knew the matter but not the heart."
The sage is prepared for both.
The Grand Steward of Sòng was powerful and controlled decisions.
Jì Zǐ was about to meet the ruler of Sòng.
Liáng Zǐ heard of it and said:
"His words must allow me to sit as an equal with the Grand Steward,
otherwise
he will not escape harm."
Therefore, Jì Zǐ spoke of valuing the ruler
and slighting the state.
Yáng Zhū's younger brother, Yáng Bù, went out wearing white clothes.
It rained,
so he took off the white clothes,
put on black clothes, and returned home.
His dog did not recognize him and barked at him.
Yáng Bù was angry
and was about to strike it.
Yáng Zhū said:
"Do not strike it.
You are the same.
If you had sent your dog out white
and it had come back black,
how could you not be surprised?"
Huì Zǐ said:
"When Yì holds the aiming-peg and bow,
operates the crossbow mechanism,
the people of Yuè compete to be his target holders.
When a weak child pulls a bow,
a loving mother enters the room and closes the door."
Therefore it is said:
"If it is certain,
then the people of Yuè do not doubt Yì;
if it is uncertain,
then a loving mother flees from her weak child."
Duke Huán asked Guǎn Zhòng:
"Is there a limit to wealth?"
He replied:
"Only water has a limit
when there is no water.
Only wealth has a limit
when one's wealth is already sufficient.
People cannot stop themselves at sufficiency
and thus perish;
is this not the limit to wealth?"
There was a wealthy merchant of Sòng named Jiān Zhǐ Zǐ.
He competed with someone to buy a hundred-*jīn* piece of uncut jade.
He then pretended to drop and break it,
bearing the hundred-*jīn* loss,
and examined the broken flaws,
gaining a thousand *yì* from it.
Sometimes there are affairs that, when undertaken, result in failure,
and one praises not undertaking them;
this is the time to bear the loss.
Someone wanted to use his chariot driving skills to be presented to the king of Jīng,
but the other drivers were jealous.
So they said:
"He can startle deer."
He was presented to the king.
The king served as the driver,
but could not catch up to the deer;
when he drove himself,
he caught up to it.
The king admired his driving,
but the driver then said that the other drivers were jealous of him.
The order came from Jīng for the young master to attack Chén.
An old man saw him off, saying:
"Jìn is strong;
you must be careful."
The young master said:
"Why does the old man worry?
I will defeat Jìn for the old man."
The old man said:
"Very well.
I will build a hut outside the south gate of Chén."
The young master said:
"Why is that?"
He said:
"I am laughing at Gōujiàn.
For someone to make others so easily surrender,
why did he alone exert himself in secret for ten difficult years?"
Yáo wanted to yield the empire to Xǔ Yóu.
Xǔ Yóu fled from him,
staying at the house of a family,
and the family hid his leather cap.
To abandon the empire
yet have one's leather cap hidden by a family
is not to understand Xǔ Yóu.
Three lice were in dispute with each other.
Another louse passed by
and said:
"What are you disputing about?"
The three lice said:
"We are fighting over fertile land."
The louse said:
"You do not even worry about the arrival of the sacrifice
and the dryness of the thatch;
what else do you have to worry about?"
Thereupon, they gathered together and bit their host
and ate it.
The pig became emaciated,
so people did not kill it.
There is an insect called *guǐ*,
with one body and two mouths,
fighting over food and biting each other.
They eventually killed each other,
thus committing suicide.
Ministers who fight over affairs and destroy their state
are all like the *guǐ* insect.
If a palace is whitewashed and utensils are washed,
then they are clean.
Conducting oneself is also like this;
if there is no place for washing away faults,
then there will be few mistakes.
Young Master Jiū was about to cause trouble,
so Duke Huán sent a messenger to observe him.
The messenger reported back, saying:
"His laughter is not joyful,
and his gaze is unfocused;
he will certainly cause trouble."
Thereupon he had the men of Lǔ kill him.
Gōngsūn Hóng cut his hair and became a cavalryman for the king of Yuè.
Gōngsūn Xǐ sent someone to break off relations with him, saying:
"I will no longer be brothers with you."
Gōngsūn Hóng said:
"I cut my hair,
but you cut off heads to use soldiers for others;
what shall I say to you?"
In the battle of Zhōu Nán,
Gōngsūn Xǐ died there.
Someone had a violent person as a neighbor
and wanted to sell his house and avoid him.
Someone said:
"His string of cash is about to be full."
He said:
"Very well,
I will wait for him."
He replied,
"I fear that he wants to use me to fulfill his ambition."
So he left.
Therefore it is said,
"What is close to being seized
is not what is desired."
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said to his disciples,
"Who can guide Zǐxī 子西 to fish for fame?"
Zǐgòng 子貢 said,
"Sì 賜 can."
So he guided him,
and he no longer had doubts.
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said,
"How generous!
He is not swayed by profit.
How pure!
The nature of the people is constant.
Crooked is crooked,
straight is straight."
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said,
"Zǐxī 子西 will not escape."
In the Bái Gōng 白公 rebellion,
Zǐxī 子西 died.
Therefore it is said,
"Those who are straight in action are crooked in desire."
Zhōng Xíng Wénzǐ 中行文子 of Jìn 晉 was fleeing into exile,
passing through a district.
His follower said,
"This is the tax collector,
an old friend of yours.
Why don't you stop and rest?
And wait for the carriages behind?"
Wénzǐ 文子 said,
"I once liked music,
and this man gave me a zither;
I liked pendants,
and this man gave me jade rings:
these are things to cover up my faults.
He is seeking favor with me,
and I fear that he will use me to seek favor with others."
So he left.
Indeed, he collected two of Wénzǐ's 文子 following carriages
and presented them to his lord.
Zhōu Zào 周趮 said to Gōng Tuō 宮他,
"Tell the King of Qí 齊 for me,
'If Qí 齊 funds me in Wèi 魏,
I will serve you with Wèi 魏.'"
Gōng Tuō 宮他 said,
"That is not possible.
It shows that there is no Wèi 魏.
The King of Qí 齊 will surely not fund one without Wèi 魏,
and will resent one with Wèi 魏.
You should rather say,
'With what the King desires,
I will obey the King with Wèi 魏.'
The King of Qí 齊 will surely think that you have Wèi 魏,
and will surely rely on you.
Then you will have Qí 齊,
and thus have both Qí 齊
and Wèi 魏."
Bái Guī 白圭 said to the Grand Governor of Sòng 宋,
"If the ruler can govern himself,
you will have nothing to do.
Now that the ruler is young and seeks fame,
you should rather have Jīng 荊 congratulate the ruler on his filial piety,
then the ruler will not take away your position,
and will greatly respect you,
so you will always be able to use Sòng 宋."
Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 and Bào Shū 鮑叔 said to each other,
"The ruler is extremely chaotic,
and will surely lose the state.
Among the sons of the ruler of Qí 齊 who can be assisted,
there is either Gōngzǐ Jiū 公子糾
or Xiǎobái 小白.
Let us each serve one,
and whoever succeeds first will take in the other."
Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 then followed Gōngzǐ Jiū 公子糾,
and Bào Shū 鮑叔 followed Xiǎobái 小白.
The people of the state indeed killed the ruler.
Xiǎobái 小白 entered first and became the ruler,
the people of Lǔ 魯 detained Guǎn Zhòng 管仲 and offered him up,
but Bào Shū 鮑叔 spoke up for him and made him prime minister.
Therefore, the proverb says,
"Even if the shaman Xián 咸 is good at blessings,
he cannot purify himself.
Even if the doctor of Qín 秦 is good at removing disease,
he cannot cure himself."
Even with the wisdom of Guǎn Zhòng 管仲,
he still needed the help of Bào Shū 鮑叔.
This is what the vulgar proverb means
"A barbarian selling his own fur coat cannot sell it,
and a scholar praising his own eloquence is not believed."
The King of Jīng 荊 attacked Wú 吳,
Wú 吳 sent Jū Wèi 沮衛 and Jué Róng 蹶融 to present gifts to the Jīng 荊 army,
and the general said,
"Tie them up
and kill them to consecrate the drums."
He asked them,
"Did you come
to divine?"
They replied,
"We did divine."
"Was the divination auspicious?"
They said,
"It was auspicious."
The Jīng 荊 man said,
"Now the Jīng 荊 general wants to kill you to consecrate the drums,
what does that mean?"
They replied,
"That is the reason why it was auspicious.
When the Wú 吳 envoy came,
they certainly observed the general's anger.
If the general is angry,
he will build deep trenches and high ramparts;
if the general is not angry,
he will be lax.
Now
if the general kills us,
then Wú 吳 will surely be alert.
Moreover, the divination of the state
is not for the sake of one official.
To kill one official to save a state,
why would that not be called auspicious?
Moreover, if the dead have no knowledge,
then using us to consecrate the drums is useless;
if the dead have knowledge,
then we will, at the time of battle,
make the drums not sound."
The Jīng 荊 man therefore did not kill them.
Zhì Bó 智伯 was about to attack Chóu Yóu 仇由,
but the road was difficult and impassable,
so he cast a large bell and sent it as a gift to the ruler of Chóu Yóu 仇由.
The ruler of Chóu Yóu 仇由 was very happy
and cleared the road to bring it in.
Chì Zhāng Mànzhī 赤章曼枝 said,
"That is not possible.
This is how the small serve the great,
but now the great comes to us,
soldiers will surely follow,
it must not be allowed in."
The ruler of Chóu Yóu 仇由 did not listen
and brought it in.
Chì Zhāng Mànzhī 赤章曼枝 then broke the chariot axle and fled
to Qí 齊.
Seven months later, Chóu Yóu 仇由 was destroyed.
Yuè 越 had already defeated Wú 吳
and again demanded soldiers from Jīng 荊 to attack Jìn 晉.
The Left Historian Yǐ Xiāng 倚相 said to the King of Jīng 荊,
"When Yuè 越 defeated Wú 吳,
the heroes died,
the elite soldiers were exhausted,
and the heavy armor was damaged.
Now they demand soldiers again to attack Jìn 晉,
showing that they are not sick.
It is better to raise an army and divide Wú 吳 with them."
The King of Jīng 荊 said,
"Good."
So he raised an army and followed Yuè 越.
The King of Yuè 越 was angry
and was about to attack them.
Grand Tutor Zhǒng 種 said,
"That is not possible.
Our heroes are exhausted,
and our heavy armor is damaged.
If we fight them,
we will surely not prevail,
it is better to bribe them."
So he ceded five hundred *lǐ* 里 south of Lùshān 露山
to bribe them.
Jīng 荊 attacked Chén 陳,
Wú 吳 rescued them,
the armies were thirty *lǐ* 里 apart.
It rained for ten days,
the night was starry.
Zuǒ Shǐ Yǐ Xiāng said to Zǐ Qī:
"If it rains for ten days,
armor will be gathered and soldiers assembled.
The Wú people will surely arrive,
it is better to prepare for them."
So he arranged a battle formation.
Before the formation was completed, the Wú people arrived,
saw the Jīng formation, and retreated.
Zuǒ Shǐ said:
"The Wú retreated sixty *lǐ*,
their lords must rest,
and their commoners must eat.
If we march thirty *lǐ* and attack them,
we can surely defeat them."
So they followed his advice
and defeated the Wú army.
Hán and Zhào were having difficulties with each other.
The Hán ruler asked for soldiers from Wèi, saying:
"I wish to borrow troops to attack Zhào."
Wèi Wén Hóu said:
"I am like a brother to Zhào,
I cannot comply."
Zhào then asked for soldiers to attack Hán.
Wén Hóu said:
"I am like a brother to Hán,
I dare not comply."
The two states could not get soldiers,
became angry, and turned against him.
Later, they realized that Wén Hóu was using them to build trust with himself,
so they both paid tribute to Wèi.
Qí attacked Lǔ,
demanding the *chán* tripod,
so Lǔ sent them a goose.
The Qí people said:
"It is a goose."
The Lǔ people said:
"It is genuine."
Qí said:
"Send Yuèzhèng Zǐchūn here,
and we will listen to you."
The Lǔ ruler asked Yuèzhèng Zǐchūn,
Yuèzhèng Zǐchūn said:
"Why not send the real one?"
The ruler said:
"I cherish it."
He replied:
"I also cherish my integrity."
Hán Jiù was established as ruler but not yet settled.
His younger brother was in Zhōu,
Zhōu wanted to give him importance,
but feared that Hán Jiù would not be established.
Qímǔ Huī said:
"It would be better to send him off with a hundred chariots.
If he is established,
claim it was a precautionary escort;
if he is not established,
then claim he came to offer the rebel."
Jìng Guō Jūn was about to build a city in Xuē,
and many guests tried to dissuade him.
Jìng Guō Jūn said to the gatekeeper:
"Do not let any guests through."
A man from Qí requested to see him, saying:
"I only ask to say three words.
If I exceed three words,
I will submit to being boiled."
Jìng Guō Jūn then saw him.
The guest hurried forward and said:
"Sea, big fish."
Then he turned and ran away.
Jìng Guō Jūn said:
"Please explain what you mean."
The guest said:
"I dare not jest with death."
Jìng Guō Jūn said:
"I wish you would tell me."
He replied:
"Have you heard of the big fish?
Nets cannot stop it,
and arrows cannot snag it.
But when it is stranded and loses water,
even ants can have their way with it.
Now, Qí is your sea.
If you always have Qí,
what need is there for Xuē?
If you lose Qí,
even if you build the walls of Xuē as high as the sky,
it will still be useless."
Jìng Guō Jūn said:
"Good."
So he stopped
and did not build the city of Xuē.
The younger brother of the Jīng king was in Qín,
but Qín would not release him.
A *zhòng shè* official said:
"Give me a hundred *jīn*,
and I can get him out."
So he loaded a hundred *jīn* and went to Jìn,
where he met Shū Xiàng,
and said:
"The younger brother of the Jīng king is in Qín,
but Qín will not release him.
Please allow me to entrust these hundred *jīn* to Shū Xiàng."
Shū Xiàng accepted the gold
and used it to petition Duke Píng of Jìn, saying:
"We can build the city of Húqiū."
Duke Píng said:
"Why is that?"
He replied:
"The younger brother of the Jīng king is in Qín,
and Qín will not release him,
which means Qín dislikes Jīng and
surely dares not forbid us from building the city of Húqiū.
If they forbid it,
we will say:
'Release the younger brother of the Jīng king for me,
and we will not build it.'
If they release him,
we can earn Jīng's gratitude;
if they do not release him,
it is their complete dislike,
and they will surely dare not forbid us from building the city of Húqiū."
The duke said:
"Good."
So he built the city of Húqiū.
He told the Duke of Qín:
"Release the younger brother of the Jīng king for me,
and we will not build it."
Qín then released him.
The Jīng king was very pleased
and gifted Jìn with a hundred *yì* of refined gold.
Hé Lǘ attacked Yǐng,
winning three victories in battle.
He asked Zǐ Xū:
"Can we retreat?"
Zǐ Xū replied:
"If a drowning man stops after one drink,
he will never finish drowning,
because he stopped.
It is better to take advantage of the situation and sink him completely."
A man from Zhèng had a son
who was about to become an official,
so he told his family:
"You must build up the dilapidated wall,
otherwise, it is not good,
and people will steal."
The neighbor also said the same thing.
They did not rebuild it in time,
and someone indeed stole from them.
They considered the son wise
and the neighbor who warned them a thief.
People of ancient times
had eyes too short to see themselves,
so they used a mirror to look at their faces;
their wisdom was too short to know themselves,
so they used the *dào* to correct themselves.
Therefore, the mirror has no fault in revealing flaws,
and the *dào* has no resentment for illuminating mistakes.
If the eyes lose the mirror,
there is no way to correct the beard and eyebrows;
if the body loses the *dào*,
there is no way to know one's confusion.
Xīmén Bào's nature was hasty,
so he wore leather to slow himself down;
Dǒng Ānyú's heart was slow,
so he wore a bowstring to urge himself on.
Therefore, using the excess to supplement the insufficient,
and using strengths to extend shortcomings,
is called a wise ruler.
There are three reliable principles in the world:
First, there are things that wisdom cannot establish;
second, there are things that strength cannot lift;
third, there are things that force cannot overcome.
Therefore, even with the wisdom of Yáo (堯),
without the help of the masses,
great achievements cannot be established.
Even with the strength of Wū Huò (烏獲),
without the assistance of others,
he cannot lift himself.
Even with the might of Bēn (賁) and Yù (育),
without methods and techniques,
one cannot achieve lasting victory.
Thus, situations can be unattainable,
and affairs can be unachievable.
Therefore, Wū Huò (烏獲) can lift a thousand *jūn* (鈞) with ease,
but finds his own body heavy;
it is not that his body is heavier than a thousand *jūn* (鈞),
but that the situation is unfavorable.
Lí Zhū (離朱) easily sees a hundred paces away,
but has difficulty seeing his own eyebrows and eyelashes;
it is not that a hundred paces are near and eyebrows and eyelashes are far,
but that the method is impossible.
Therefore, an enlightened ruler does not exhaust Wū Huò (烏獲)
by asking him to lift himself;
does not trouble Lí Zhū (離朱)
by asking him to see himself.
He takes advantage of favorable situations,
seeks easy methods,
therefore using little effort yet establishing great achievements and reputation.
Times have fullness and emptiness,
affairs have benefit and harm,
things have life and death.
If a ruler shows joy or anger over these three,
then even the most steadfast and loyal ministers will lose heart.
The simplicity of sages and worthies is profound.
Therefore, an enlightened ruler observes others,
and does not allow others to observe him.
Understanding that Yáo (堯) could not achieve things alone,
Wū Huò (烏獲) could not lift himself,
and Bēn (賁) and Yù (育) could not always win,
using laws and methods
completes the way of observation and action.
There are seven methods for maintaining stability,
and six paths to danger.
The methods for maintaining stability:
First,
rewards and punishments follow right and wrong;
second,
fortune and misfortune follow good and evil;
third,
life and death follow laws and standards;
fourth,
there are worthies and unworthies, but no personal likes or dislikes;
fifth,
there are foolish and wise, but no biased praise or blame;
sixth,
there are measurements and standards, but no subjective estimations;
seventh,
there is trustworthiness, but no deceit.
The paths to danger:
First,
to carve and trim within the guidelines of the plumb line;
second,
to make judgments and executions outside the law;
third,
to benefit what others harm;
fourth,
to delight in what brings misfortune to others;
fifth,
to endanger others in what they find secure;
sixth,
those who are loved are not close, and those who are hated are not kept distant.
If it is like this,
then people lose their joy in living,
and forget their fear of death.
If people do not rejoice in living,
then the ruler is not respected.
If they do not fear death,
then orders are not carried out.
Make everyone in the world use all their intelligence in observing appearance,
and exhaust their strength in weighing gains and losses,
so that moving leads to victory,
and being still leads to peace.
To govern the world, make people rejoice in doing what is right,
and cherish their bodies by avoiding what is wrong,
so that petty people are few and gentlemen are many.
Therefore, the state is established for a long time,
and the nation is secure for a long time.
There is no Zhòng Ní (仲尼) on a runaway chariot,
and no Bó Yí (伯夷) under an overturned boat.
Therefore, commands and orders
are the boats and chariots of the nation.
If they are secure, then wisdom and integrity arise;
if they are dangerous, then strife and baseness arise.
Therefore, the way to secure the nation
is like eating when hungry and clothing when cold—
natural without the need for commands.
The former kings entrusted principles to bamboo and silk;
their way was harmonious,
therefore later generations obeyed.
Now, if you tell people to give up being free from hunger and cold,
even Bēn (賁) and Yù (育) cannot do it;
if you abandon what is natural,
even if the way is harmonious, it cannot be established.
What strength and courage cannot accomplish
means the ruler cannot be secure.
If the ruler uses insatiable demands to blame those who have exhausted themselves,
then the subordinates will answer "nothing more".
"Nothing more"
means the law is treated lightly.
The law is what the nation relies on;
if it is treated lightly,
then accomplishments are not established,
and fame is not achieved.
I have heard that when the ancient Biǎn Què (扁鵲) treated illness,
he used knives to pierce bones;
when sages rescued a nation in danger,
they used loyal advice that grated on the ears.
Piercing bones
means small pain in the body
leads to long-term benefit for the person;
grating on the ears
means small displeasure in the heart
leads to lasting good for the nation.
Therefore, severely ill people benefit from enduring pain,
and courageous and resolute rulers benefit from advice that grates on the ears.
Enduring pain
allows Biǎn Què (扁鵲) to fully display his skill;
if ears are grated upon,
then Zǐ Xū (子胥) will not be lost.
These are the methods for prolonging life and securing peace.
If one is ill and cannot endure pain,
then the skill of Biǎn Què (扁鵲) is lost;
if one is in danger and does not accept advice that grates on the ears,
then the intention of the sages is lost.
If it is like this,
long-term benefits will not be bestowed,
and accomplishments and fame will not be established for long.
If a ruler does not discipline himself like Yáo (堯),
but demands that his ministers be as loyal as Zǐ Xū (子胥),
it is like hoping that all the Yīn (殷) people are as loyal as Bǐ Gān (比干).
If all are as loyal as Bǐ Gān (比干),
then the ruler will not fail,
and the subordinates will not perish.
Without weighing their power
and having a Tián Chéng (田成), and still hoping their loyalty is like that of Bǐ Gān (比干),
then the nation will not have a moment of peace.
Abandoning Yáo (堯) and Shùn (舜) and establishing Jié (桀) and Zhòu (紂),
then people will not be able to rejoice in their strengths
but will worry about their shortcomings.
Losing their strengths
means the nation will have no accomplishments;
clinging to their shortcomings
means the people will not rejoice in living.
Using those without accomplishment to govern those who do not rejoice in living
is not feasible among the common people.
If it is like this,
then the ruler will have no way to command the subordinates,
and the subordinates will have no way to serve the ruler.
Security or danger lies in right and wrong,
not in strength or weakness;
survival or destruction lies in substance and reality,
not in numbers.
Therefore, Qí (齊),
with ten thousand chariots,
does not have its name matching the reality.
The ruler is empty and hollow within the nation,
and is not filled with substance and reality,
therefore ministers are able to usurp the ruler.
Jié, the Son of Heaven,
was without right or wrong:
he rewarded those without merit,
causing flatterers and deceivers to be valued for their falsehoods;
he punished those without guilt,
causing hunchbacks to have their backs cut open due to their natural condition.
He regarded falsehood as right,
and natural disposition as wrong;
small gains prevailed over great ones.
An enlightened ruler strengthens his inner defenses,
therefore he does not suffer external losses;
there has never been a case of losing something nearby
without also losing something far away.
Therefore, when Zhōu seized Yīn,
they were picking up what was left behind in the courtyard.
If Yīn had not left anything behind in the court,
then Zhōu would not have dared to hope for even a hair's breadth within their borders,
let alone dare to usurp the throne?
The way of an enlightened ruler is to be loyal to the law,
and his law is loyal to his heart;
therefore, when he is present, there is order,
and when he is gone, he is missed.
Yáo had no contracts sealed with glue for his era,
yet his way was followed;
Shùn had no land to insert an awl for posterity,
yet his virtue was embraced.
To be able to establish a way in ancient times
and pass down virtue for all ages is what is meant by an enlightened ruler.
The laws established by a sagely king
have rewards sufficient to encourage good,
authority sufficient to overcome violence,
and preparations sufficient to ensure the law is perfectly upheld.
Ministers of an ordered era
are those whose merit is great and whose rank is high,
those whose strength is maximized and whose rewards are generous,
and those whose sincerity is exhausted and whose names are established.
The growth of good is like spring,
and the death of evil is like autumn,
therefore the people are encouraged to maximize their strength
and happily exhaust their sincerity;
this is what is meant by harmony between superiors and inferiors.
With harmony between superiors and inferiors,
one can employ those who exert their strength to the utmost in matters of measurement and standards,
and strive to reach the level of Rèn Bǐ;
soldiers go to their deaths
and wish to be like Bēn and Yù;
those who uphold the Way all cherish hearts of metal and stone,
and are willing to die with the integrity of Zǐ Xū.
If those who exert their strength are like Rèn Bǐ,
those who fight are like Bēn and Yù,
and those who are loyal are like metal and stone,
then the ruler can sleep soundly
and his defense is complete.
The good defenders of old
used what they valued to prohibit what they considered trivial,
and used what was difficult to stop what was easy.
Therefore, both gentlemen and petty men were upright,
and even Dào Zhí was as honest as Zēng and Shǐ.
How do we know this?
For greedy thieves would not jump into a ravine to pick up gold,
for jumping into a ravine to pick up gold
would endanger their lives.
Bēn and Yù would not have a reputation for bravery if they did not assess their enemies;
Dào Zhí would not achieve his gains if he did not calculate what was possible.
The prohibitions of an enlightened ruler
are such that Bēn and Yù find themselves invaded in areas they cannot conquer,
and Dào Zhí sees harm in what he cannot take.
Therefore, being able to prohibit what Bēn and Yù cannot violate
and defend against what Dào Zhí cannot take,
then the violent will be compliant
and the wicked will return to righteousness.
When the greatly brave are compliant
and the master thief is honest,
then the world is fair
and the feelings of the common people are upright.
If a ruler departs from the law
and loses the people,
he will be in danger of the fate of Bó Yí, who would not take what was not his,
and will not escape the disasters of Tián Chéng and Dào Zhí,
why is that?
Today, there is not a single Bó Yí in the world,
but treacherous people never disappear from the world,
therefore establish laws and measures.
If measures are reliable,
then Bó Yí will not lose what is right,
and Dào Zhí will not get what is wrong.
If the laws are clear,
then the virtuous cannot be deprived by the unworthy,
the strong cannot encroach upon the weak,
and the many cannot tyrannize the few.
Entrusting the world to the laws of Yáo,
then the virtuous will not lose their share,
and the treacherous will not seek good fortune.
Attaching a thousand gold pieces to Yì's arrow,
then Bó Yí cannot lose it,
and Dào Zhí will not dare to take it.
Yáo was wise in not losing the treacherous,
therefore the world had no evil;
Yì was skillful in not missing his shot,
therefore the thousand gold pieces were not lost.
The treacherous do not live long, and Dào Zhí is stopped.
Because of this,
the map does not depict Zǎi Yǔ,
nor does it elevate the Six Ministers;
the book does not record Zǐ Xū,
nor does it illuminate Fūchāi.
The strategies of Sūn and Wú are discarded,
and the heart of Dào Zhí is subdued.
The ruler happily resides in the jade hall,
without the worries of angry glares or attempts to usurp;
the ministers stand with folded hands within the golden city,
without the calamities of being seized by the wrist or whispering in lament.
To tame a tiger without a cage,
to prevent treachery without law,
to block falsehood without seals—
these are the worries of Bēn and Yù,
and the difficulties of Yáo and Shùn.
Therefore, setting up a cage
is not to prepare for mice,
but to enable the timid to subdue tigers;
establishing laws
is not to prepare for Zēng and Shǐ,
but to enable mediocre rulers to stop Dào Zhí;
creating seals
is not to anticipate Wěi Shēng,
but to prevent people from deceiving each other.
Do not solely rely on Bǐ Gān's death for integrity,
or hope for the absence of treachery from rebellious ministers;
rely on what the timid can subdue
and grasp what mediocre rulers can easily defend.
In the present age,
to devise loyal plans for the ruler
and establish virtue for the world,
nothing is more beneficial than this.
Therefore, the ruler will have no plans for destroying the country,
and the loyal minister will have no schemes for losing his life.
Be clear that high position will surely be rewarded,
so that people can be made to maximize their strength in matters of measurement and standards
and die for their integrity in their official duties.
Understand the feelings of Bēn and Yù,
not exchanging life for death;
be wary of the greed of Dào Zhí,
not exchanging wealth for life,
then the way to defend the country is fully prepared.
It is said that those in ancient times who were good at employing people
necessarily followed Heaven and obeyed man
and clearly administered rewards and punishments.
Following Heaven
results in little effort but established merit;
obeying man
results in fewer penalties and executed orders;
clarifying rewards and punishments
results in no confusion between Bó Yí and Dào Zhí.
Like this,
then black and white are distinguished.
Ministers who govern the country
demonstrate merit in the country to ascend to position,
show ability in their office to receive a job,
and exhaust their strength in matters of measurement and standards
to handle affairs.
The ministers should all suit their abilities,
be competent in their offices,
and lighten their duties,
and no one should harbor excess strength in their hearts,
nor should they bear the responsibility of holding multiple positions for the ruler.
Therefore, there will be no internal rebellions of suppressed resentment
nor external disasters like Mǎ Fú.
An enlightened ruler ensures that affairs do not interfere with each other,
therefore there are no lawsuits;
ensures that officials do not hold multiple positions,
therefore skills are developed;
ensures that people do not perform the same tasks,
therefore there is no competition.
When disputes and lawsuits cease,
and skills are developed,
then the strong and weak do not test their strength,
ice and charcoal do not combine,
and no one in the world can harm each other;
this is the height of governance.
If you abandon law and methods and govern with your heart,
Yáo 堯 could not govern even one state properly.
If you discard compasses and rulers and guess with your own mind,
Xī Zhòng 奚仲 could not make a single wheel.
If you abolish measurements and arbitrarily decide lengths,
Wáng Ěr 王爾 could not even hit half the target.
If you have a mediocre ruler uphold law and methods,
