When Duke Huán of Zhèng was about to attack Kuài,
he first inquired about the heroes, good ministers, and clever and brave men of Kuài,
and obtained all their names.
He chose good fields in Kuài to bribe them with,
and wrote down the titles of offices.
Then he set up an altar outside the city gate
and buried the documents,
sacrificing a rooster and a boar,
as if making a covenant.
The ruler of Kuài thought it was internal strife
and killed all his good ministers.
Duke Huán of Zhèng attacked Kuài
and consequently captured it.
Xiāng Cī, the magistrate of Yè,
secretly befriended the attendants of the King of Zhào.
When the King of Zhào plotted to attack Yè,
Xiāng Cī would always hear of it
and inform the King of Wèi first.
The King of Wèi prepared for it,
and Zhào then ceased the attack.
Tactics Seven: 〓#
A dwarf of Qín was on good terms with the King of Jīng,
and secretly befriended the attendants of the King of Jīng
and was highly regarded by King Huìwén.
Whenever Jīng had a plan,
the dwarf would always hear of it first
and inform King Huìwén.
During the time of Lord Sì of Wèi,
there was someone among the magistrate's attendants.
The county magistrate opened his rush mat
and found the matting to be very worn.
Lord Sì then sent someone to give him a mat,
saying,
"I heard that you recently opened your rush mat
and found the matting to be very worn,
so I give you this mat."
The county magistrate was greatly surprised
and considered his lord to be a god.
Principle One: 〓#
The way of a discerning ruler
is like Yǒu Ruò responding to Mì Zǐ.
When a ruler listens to words,
he praises their eloquence;
when he observes actions,
he values their far-reaching effects.
Therefore, the words of ministers, scholars, and commoners
are often circuitous and grand,
and their conduct
is often detached from the world.
The explanation lies in Tián Jiū's response to the King of Jīng.
Therefore, Mò Zǐ made a wooden kite,
and Ōu Guī built the Wǔ Palace.
Medicine, wine, and loyal advice
are understood by the discerning ruler and sage ruler through unique insight.
Principle Two: 〓#
If a ruler does not use effectiveness as the standard when listening to advice,
then speakers
will often give thorny and white horse sophistries;
if a ruler does not use a consistent target as a standard,
then all archers will be like Yì.
A ruler's attitude towards advice
is like that of the King of Yàn learning the Way;
and those who give lengthy advice
are all like the people of Zhèng arguing about age.
Therefore, if words are subtle and hard to discern
but not focused on practical matters,
then Jì, Huì, Sòng, and Mò are all just drawing plans;
if discussions are circuitous, profound, and grand
but not useful,
then Wèi, Cháng, Zhān, Chén, and Zhuāng are all just ghosts and spirits;
if actions are contrary, difficult, and firm
but not effective,
then Wù, Biàn, Bào, Jiè, and Tián Zhòng are all just hard gourds.
Furthermore, if Yú Qìng scolds the craftsman, the house will collapse,
and if Fàn Qiě exhausts the craftsman, the bow will break.
Therefore, when seeking sincerity,
returning gifts is indispensable.
The Third Canon: 〓#
If forced to act for another, then there will be blame and expectations;
if acting for oneself, then affairs will proceed.
Thus, fathers and sons sometimes resent each other's nagging;
those who take hirelings and artisans advance fine soups.
The explanation lies in Wén Gōng's 文公 prior declarations
and Gōu Jiàn's 勾踐 proclamations "like an emperor."
Therefore, Húan Gōng 桓公 concealed his anger at Cài 蔡 and attacked Chǔ 楚;
Wú Qǐ 吳起 harbored ulcers and sucked wounds.
Moreover, the odes and eulogies of the former kings,
the inscriptions on bells and tripods,
all broadcast our deeds,
as vast as Mount Húashān 華山.
Yet, what the former kings expected was profit;
what they employed was strength.
The proverb about building a shrine
is self-explanatory.
May I suggest that scholars
pursue devious means from the former kings;
or perhaps it is not suitable for today?
If so,
it cannot be changed.
A man from Zhèng 鄭 county got stuck with a cart;
a man from Wèi 衛 assisted Yì 弋;
Bǔ Zǐ's 卜子 wife wrote on worn-out trousers;
and the younger one attended the elder one in drinking.
The words of the former kings
have things that are small in what they do
but great in the world's intention,
and things that are great in what they do
but small in the world's intention;
it cannot necessarily be known.
The explanation lies in the Sòng 宋 person's interpretation of the *Shū* 書 (Book of Documents),
and the Liáng 梁 person's reading of the *Jì* 記 (Book of Rites).
Therefore, the former kings had Yǐng 郢 writings,
but later generations had many Yān 燕 interpretations.
Those who do not suit the affairs of the state but plan for the former kings
are all going back to take measurements.
The Fourth Canon: 〓#
Where profit lies, the people flock;
where fame shines, the scholars die for it.
Therefore, if merit is outside the law and rewards are added,
then the ruler cannot obtain what he profits from his subjects;
if fame is outside the law and praise is added,
then the scholars encourage fame and do not store it up for the ruler.
Therefore, Zhōng Zhāng 中章 and Xū Jǐ 胥己 served,
and the people of Zhōngmóu 中牟 abandoned fields and gardens and followed literary scholars, half the town;
Píng Gōng's 平公 leg hurt and his foot was numb, but
he did not dare to break his sitting posture;
the number of those in Jìn 晉 state who resigned from office and entrusted things to others was half the state.
These three scholars,
if their words followed the law,
then they were recorded in official registers;
if their actions were within affairs,
then they were like the law-abiding people;
the rituals of the two lords were too excessive.
If their words departed from the law and their actions were distant merits,
then they were people outside the rules;
why would the two lords give them rituals?
The rituals should be eliminated.
Moreover, scholars who reside in learning,
when the state has no affairs, do not use their strength;
when there is difficulty, they do not wear armor.
If they are given rituals,
then they will be lazy in cultivating the merits of farming and war;
if they are not given rituals,
then they will harm the ruler's laws.
If the state is peaceful, then they are honored and prominent;
if it is in danger, then they become the authority of Qū Gōng 屈公.
What does the ruler gain from scholars who reside in learning?
Therefore, an enlightened ruler discusses Lǐ Cī's 李疵 vision of Zhōngshān 中山.
The Fifth Canon: 〓#
The *Shī* 詩 (Book of Poetry) says:
"If you do not do it yourself and are not personally involved,
the common people will not believe."
Fù Yuè's 傅說 example is using
"no purple clothing";
the support is Zhèng Jiǎn 鄭簡 and Sòng Xiāng 宋襄;
the demands are respecting and valuing farming and war.
If one does not clarify duties,
does not demand sincerity,
and personally occupies a position below,
and even runs errands and sleeps and rests for those below,
it is the same as hiding defects and wearing inconspicuous clothing.
Kǒng Qiū 孔丘 did not understand,
therefore he claimed [the state of Lǔ 魯] was like a vessel;
the ruler of Zōu 鄒 did not understand,
therefore he first brought disgrace upon himself.
The way of an enlightened ruler
is like Shū Xiàng's 叔向 hunting ode,
and Zhāo Hóu's 昭侯 listening.
The Sixth Canon: 〓#
If small trustworthiness is established,
then great trustworthiness is established;
therefore, an enlightened ruler accumulates trustworthiness.
If rewards and punishments are not trustworthy,
then prohibitions and orders will not be carried out.
The explanation lies in Wén Gōng's 文公 attack on Yuán 原,
and Jī Zhèng's 箕鄭 rescue of the starving.
Therefore, Wú Qǐ 吳起 waited for an old friend to eat;
Wén Hóu 文侯 met with a forester to hunt.
Therefore, an enlightened ruler displays trustworthiness,
like Zēng Zǐ 曾子 killing a pig.
The worry is Lì Wáng's 厲王 beating the alarm drum,
and Lǐ Kuī's 李悝 deceiving two reconcilers.
The First Explanation: 〓#
Mì Zǐjiàn 宓子賤 governed Dānfù 單父.
Yǒu Ruò 有若 saw him and said:
"Why are you so emaciated?"
Mì Zǐ said:
"The ruler does not know that I am unworthy,
and made me govern Dānfù 單父.
Official matters are urgent,
and my heart is worried,
therefore I am emaciated."
Yǒu Ruò 有若 said:
"In the past, Shùn 舜 played the five-stringed zither,
and sang the *Nán Fēng* 南風 (South Wind) poem,
and the world was governed.
Now, even with the small matter of Dānfù 單父,
you govern it with worry;
how will you govern the world?
Therefore, if you have the methods to control it,
you can sit in the ancestral hall,
and have the appearance of a young maiden,
and it will not harm the governing;
if you do not have the methods to control it,
even if you are exhausted and emaciated,
it will still not be beneficial."
The king of Chǔ 楚 said to Tián Jiū 田鳩:
"Mòzǐ 墨子 is
a prominent school of thought.
His body is capable,
but his words are many and not well-reasoned.
Why is that?"
He said:
"In the past, the Bó 伯 of Qín 秦 married his daughter to the Gōngzǐ 公子 of Jìn 晉,
ordering Jìn 晉 to prepare the dowry for her,
following her with seventy people as concubines with embroidered clothes.
When they arrived in Jìn 晉,
the people of Jìn 晉 loved the concubines and despised the princess.
This can be said to be good at marrying off the concubines,
but it cannot be said to be good at marrying off the daughter.
A person from Chǔ 楚 had to sell his pearls in Zhèng 鄭,
making a case of magnolia wood,
perfuming it with cinnamon and pepper,
stringing it with pearls and jade,
adorning it with rubies,
and embellishing it with emeralds.
The people of Zhèng 鄭 bought the case and returned the pearls.
This can be said to be good at selling the case,
but it cannot be said to be good at selling the pearls.
Today's discussions
all talk about eloquent language and literary expressions;
the rulers examine their writing and forget its usefulness.
Mòzǐ's 墨子 doctrines
transmit the ways of the former kings,
and discuss the words of the sages
to proclaim them to the people.
If one were to argue about its language,
then I fear people would cherish its writing
and forget its directness,
using the writing to harm its usefulness.
This is the same type of thing as the person from Chǔ 楚 selling pearls
and the Bó 伯 of Qín 秦 marrying off his daughter,
therefore his words are many and not well-reasoned."
Mòzǐ 墨子 made a wooden kite,
taking three years to complete,
and it flew for one day before breaking.
His disciples said:
"Master's skill
is so great that he can make a wooden kite fly."
Mòzǐ 墨子 said:
"I am not as skilled as the one who makes the *chē ní* 車輗 (linchpin) for carts.
Using a foot of wood,
without spending a morning's work,
to lift the burden of thirty *dàn*,
achieving distant strength with much,
lasting for many years.
Now I make a kite,
it takes three years to complete,
but it is ruined in a single day."
*Huìzǐ* heard this and said:
"*Mòzǐ* is very skillful,
skillful in making *ní*,
clumsy in making kites."
The *Sòng* king was at odds with *Qí*,
and was building the *Wǔ* Palace.
*Ōuguǐ* led the singing,
passers-by stopped to watch,
and the builders did not tire.
The king heard of this,
summoned him and rewarded him.
He replied:
"My teacher *Shèjī*'s singing
is even better than *Guǐ*'s."
The king summoned *Shèjī* and had him sing,
passers-by did not stop,
and the builders felt tired.
The king said:
"Passers-by do not stop,
and the builders feel tired,
his singing is not as beautiful as *Guǐ*'s,
why is that?"
He replied:
"Your Majesty, please measure their work."
*Guǐ* achieved four planks,
*Shèjī* eight planks;
test their firmness,
*Guǐ* was five *cùn*,
*Shèjī* was two *cùn*.
Good medicine is bitter to the taste,
but the wise man advises and drinks it,
knowing that it will cure his illness.
Loyal words grate on the ear,
but the enlightened ruler listens to them,
knowing that they can lead to success.
Discourse Two: 〓#
A *Sòng* man asked
to carve a monkey on the tip of a thorn for the King of *Yān*;
he required three months of purification,
before one could observe it.
The King of *Yān* therefore supported him with three chariots.
The master craftsman on the right said to the king:
"I have heard that rulers do not abstain from pleasure for even ten days.
Now I know that the king cannot abstain for long
to observe a useless object,
so he set the deadline at three months.
All carvers
use something smaller to carve.
Now, I am a metalworker,
and I have nothing to carve it with,
this is an impossible object,
the king must investigate it."
The king then imprisoned and questioned him,
and indeed it was a fraud,
so he killed him.
The metalworker said to the king:
"If calculations lack measure,
eloquent speakers will have many thorn-tip tales."
Another version: 〓#
The King of *Yān* loved subtle crafts.
A man from *Wèi* said:
"I can carve a monkey on the tip of a thorn."
The King of *Yān* was pleased,
and supported him with the allowance of five chariots.
The king said:
"I will observe
the guest carve a monkey on the thorn."
The guest said:
"If the ruler wishes to observe it,
he must not enter the palace for half a year,
nor drink wine or eat meat.
When the rain clears and the sun comes out,
observe it in the hazy sunlight,
and the thorn-tip monkey may be seen."
The King of *Yān* supported the *Wèi* man,
but could not observe his monkey.
A metalworker from beneath the terrace in *Zhèng*
said to the King of *Yān*:
"I
am a carver.
All minute objects must be carved with a tool,
and the tool must be larger than what is carved.
Now, the tip of a thorn cannot accommodate a carving blade,
it is difficult to work on the tip of a thorn.
The king should observe the guest's carving tool,
and whether he can do it will be known."
The king said:
"Good."
He said to the *Wèi* man:
"Guest, to carve a monkey on a thorn,
what do you use to work on it?"
He said:
"With a carving tool."
The king said:
"I wish to see it."
The guest said:
"I will go to my lodging to retrieve it."
And then he fled.
*Ér Yuè*,
a man from *Sòng*,
was skilled in debate,
holding that
"a white horse is not a horse,"
he convinced the debaters of *Jìxià* in *Qí*.
Riding a white horse and passing through the gate,
he still paid the tax for a white horse.
Therefore, relying on empty words
he could conquer a state,
but examining reality and pressing the form,
he could not deceive even one person.
Sharpening a new whetstone and testing arrows,
cocking the crossbow and shooting,
even if blindly firing,
its tip will never fail to hit an autumn hair,
yet no one can recover its location,
so it cannot be called good shooting,
there is no constant target.
Setting up a five-*cùn* target,
drawing back ten paces,
only *Yì* and *Pángméng* can surely hit it completely,
because there is a constant target.
It is difficult to have a standard,
but easy to have no standard.
With a constant target,
*Yì* and *Pángméng* are skilled with the five *cùn*;
without a constant target,
then hitting an autumn hair by blindly firing
is clumsy.
Therefore, responding without a standard,
debaters will proliferate arguments;
setting up a standard and holding to it,
even the knowledgeable fear making mistakes,
and dare not speak rashly.
Now rulers listen to arguments,
not responding with a standard, but praising their eloquence;
not measuring by achievement,
but praising their conduct without entering the gate.
This is why rulers are long deceived,
and why arguers are long nourished.
A guest taught the King of *Yān* the way to immortality,
the king sent someone to learn it,
but before the person sent could learn it,
the guest died.
The king was furious
and executed him.
The king did not realize that the guest had deceived him,
but blamed the student for being slow.
To believe in impossible things
and execute innocent officials,
is the trouble of not investigating.
Moreover, what people are most concerned about
is nothing more than their own body,
if they cannot make themselves immortal,
how can they make the king live forever?
Men of *Zhèng* were arguing about their age,
one man said:
"I am the same age as *Yáo*."
The other man said:
"I am the same age as the elder brother of the Yellow Emperor."
Arguing this without resolution,
the one who stops breathing last wins.
A guest once painted a bamboo slip for Jū Jūn 周君,
and it took three years to complete.
Jū Jūn 周君 looked at it,
and it appeared the same as a lacquered bamboo slip,
so Jū Jūn 周君 was very angry.
The painter of the bamboo slip said,
"Build a wall ten boards high,
cut an eight-foot window,
and when the sun first rises,
place it there and look at it."
Jū Jūn 周君 did as he said,
and when he looked at its form,
it entirely became dragons, snakes, birds, beasts, carriages, and horses,
all sorts of things were fully present,
and Jū Jūn 周君 was very pleased.
This bamboo slip's workmanship was not at all insignificant and difficult,
but its use was the same as a plain lacquered bamboo slip.
A guest once painted for Qí Wáng 齊王.
Qí Wáng 齊王 asked,
"What is the most difficult thing to paint?"
He said,
"Dogs and horses are difficult."
"What is the easiest?"
He replied,
"Ghosts and goblins are the easiest."
Dogs and horses
are known to people,
appearing fully before them morning and night,
and cannot be misrepresented,
therefore they are difficult.
Ghosts and goblins
are formless,
and do not appear fully before them,
therefore they are easy.
In Qí 齊, there was a recluse named Tián Zhòng 田仲.
Qū Gǔ 屈穀, a man of Sòng 宋, saw him,
and said,
"I have heard of your principle, sir,
of not relying on others for food.
Now I have a giant gourd,
as hard as stone,
thick and without holes,
which I offer to you."
Tián Zhòng 田仲 said,
"What is valued in a gourd
is that it can be used to hold things.
Now it is thick and without holes,
so it cannot be split to hold things;
and being as heavy as a hard stone,
it cannot be split to use for ladling,
so I have no use for the gourd."
Qū Gǔ 屈穀 said,
"Very well,
I will throw it away."
Now Tián Zhòng 田仲 does not rely on others for food,
but he is also of no benefit to the state,
so he is like that hard gourd.
Yú Qìng 虞慶 was building a house
and said to the craftsman,
"The house is too low."
The craftsman replied,
"This is a new house,
the plaster is wet and the rafters are green."
Yú Qìng 虞慶 said,
"That is not right.
Wet plaster is heavy and green rafters are pliant;
using pliant rafters to support heavy plaster,
it should be low."
After a long time,
the plaster will dry and the rafters will season.
Dry plaster is light,
and seasoned rafters are straight;
using straight rafters to support light plaster,
it will be higher."
The craftsman was refuted
and did as he was told, and the house collapsed.
Another account says:
Yú Qìng 虞慶 was about to build a house,
and the craftsman said,
"The timber is green and the plaster is wet;
green timber is pliant,
and wet plaster is heavy;
using pliant timber to support heavy plaster,
even if it is completed now,
it will surely collapse in time."
Yú Qìng 虞慶 said,
"Seasoned timber is straight,
and dry plaster is light.
If we can have it dry now,
it will become lighter and straighter day by day,
and even after a long time,
it will surely not collapse."
The craftsman was refuted,
built it, and after a while, the house indeed collapsed.
Fàn Qiě 范且 said,
"A bow breaks
invariably at its limit,
not at its beginning.
When a craftsman strings a bow,
he places it under pressure on a frame for thirty days and then steps on the string,
releasing the mechanism in one day;
this is moderating its beginning
and hurrying its end,
how can it not break?
Stringing a bow should not be done this way.
Place it under pressure on a frame for one day and then step on the string,
releasing the mechanism in thirty days;
this is hurrying its beginning
and moderating its end."
The craftsman was at his wit's end,
did as he was told,
and the bow broke.
The words of Fàn Qiě 范且 and Yú Qìng 虞慶
were all eloquent and persuasive
but contrary to the reality of the matter.
If the ruler is pleased and does not forbid it,
this is the reason for failure.
If he does not plan for the merit of governing and strengthening the state,
but delights in the sound of eloquent and
beautiful speech,
he is rejecting those skilled in methods
and employing those who cause houses to collapse and bows to break.
Thus, in matters of state,
rulers do not understand
the construction of houses and stringing of bows.
However, those scholars who are cornered by the likes of Fàn Qiě 范且 and Yú Qìng 虞慶,
using empty words,
are useless yet prevail;
when it comes to practical matters,
they are inept and at their wit's end.
Rulers often favor useless arguments,
but lack words that are not easily refuted,
this is the reason for disorder.
Now, those in the world who act like Fàn Qiě 范且 and Yú Qìng 虞慶 do not cease,
and rulers are pleased with them without end,
which means valuing the kind of people who cause failure and breakage,
and treating those with knowledge of methods as mere craftsmen.
Craftsmen cannot apply their skills,
therefore houses collapse and bows break;
those skilled in governing cannot implement their methods,
therefore the state is disordered and the ruler is endangered.
When infants play together,
they use dust as rice,
and mud as soup,
and wood as meat,
but when evening comes, they invariably go home to eat real food,
because dust-rice and mud-soup can be used for play
but not for eating.
To praise the traditions of high antiquity,
arguing without sincerity,
speaking of the benevolence and righteousness of former kings
but being unable to govern the state properly,
this is also something that can be used for play
but not for governing.
Those who admired benevolence and righteousness but became weak and disordered
were the Three Jìn 三晉 states.
Those who did not admire it but became well-governed and strong
were Qín 秦,
but the reason they have not yet become emperors
is that their governance is not yet complete.
Discourses Three:
When people are infants,
if their parents raise them sparingly,
the children grow up and resent it.
When the children grow up to be strong adults,
if their support for their parents is meager,
the parents become angry and scold them.
Children and parents
are the closest of kin,
but the reason they sometimes scold or resent each other
is that they all have their own interests
and are not sufficiently concerned for others.
When someone hires a laborer to plow and sow,
the master spends lavishly on good food,
providing fine cloth and seeking easy payments.
It is not that they love the ordinary employer,
but they say:
"If it is like this,
the plowman will plow deeply,
and the hoe man will weed thoroughly."
The ordinary employees who devote their effort
and quickly weed and plow,
who exert all skill to straighten the fields,
do not love the master,
but say:
"If it is like this, the soup will be delicious,
and the money and cloth will be easy to obtain."
They nurture their effort and strength
with the kindness of father and son,
but their hearts are focused on their own use,
all harboring self-interest.
Therefore, when people act and give
with profit as their motive,
even people of Yuè (越) will easily be harmonious;
but with harm as their motive,
even father and son will be estranged and resentful.
Wén Gōng (文公) attacked Sòng (宋),
and first declared:
"I have heard that the ruler of Sòng (宋) is without virtue,
scorns the elders,
divides wealth unfairly,
and his orders are not trusted.
I have come to execute him for the people."
Yuè (越) attacked Wú (吳),
and first declared:
"I have heard that the King of Wú (吳) built the Terrace of Rúhuáng (如皇),
dug deep ponds,
exhausted the people,
squandered wealth,
and used up the strength of the people.
I have come to execute him for the people."
A woman from Cài (蔡) became the wife of Huán Gōng (桓公).
Huán Gōng (桓公) went on a boat with her,
and the lady rocked the boat.
Huán Gōng (桓公) was very frightened,
and when he forbade her, she did not stop,
so he angrily divorced her.
Then he planned to recall her,
but instead remarried her off to someone else.
Huán Gōng (桓公) was furious
and wanted to attack Cài (蔡).
Zhòngfù (仲父) advised him, saying:
"A game in the bedchamber
is not enough to attack a country,
and great achievements cannot be hoped for.
Please do not use this as a pretext."
Huán Gōng (桓公) did not listen.
Zhòngfù (仲父) said:
"If you must,
the Jīngmáo (菁茅) grass of Chǔ (楚) has not been offered to the Son of Heaven
for three years.
You should raise troops to attack Chǔ (楚) for the Son of Heaven.
When Chǔ (楚) submits,
take the opportunity to attack Cài (蔡),
saying:
'I am attacking Chǔ (楚) for the Son of Heaven,
and Cài (蔡) did not listen and provide troops.'"
Then destroy them.
This is righteous in name
and beneficial in reality,
so you will have the name of punishing them for the Son of Heaven
and the reality of taking revenge."
Wú Qǐ (吳起) was a general of Wèi (魏) and attacked Zhōngshān (中山).
A soldier had a boil,
and Wú Qǐ (吳起) knelt down and sucked the pus.
The mother of the wounded man stood and wept.
Someone asked, saying:
"The general treats your son like this,
why are you still weeping?"
She replied:
"Wú Qǐ (吳起) sucked the sore of his father, and his father died.
Now this son will also die,
that is why I am weeping."
The Lord of Zhào (趙), Zhǔfù (主父), ordered craftsmen to build hooked ladders
and climb up the Bōwú (播吾) mountain,
carved sparse footprints on it,
three feet wide,
and five feet long,
and inscribed on it:
"Zhǔfù (主父) often roams here."
King Zhāo (昭) of Qín (秦) ordered craftsmen to build hooked ladders
and climb up Mount Huà (華山),
using pine and cypress wood to make a chessboard,
arrows eight feet long,
chess pieces eight inches long,
and inscribed on it:
"King Zhāo (昭) once played chess with the heavenly gods here."
Wén Gōng (文公) returned to his state,
arriving at the Hé (河) River,
ordered the bamboo food containers to be thrown away,
the mats to be thrown away,
and those with calloused hands and feet and dark faces
were rewarded last.
Jiù Fàn (咎犯) heard of this and cried at night.
The Duke said:
"I fled into exile for twenty years,
and now I have returned to my state.
Jiù Fàn (咎犯) heard of this and does not rejoice but cries,
does he not want me to return to my state?"
Fàn (犯) replied:
"The bamboo food containers
are for eating,
the mats are for sleeping,
but you throw them away.
Calloused hands and feet,
dark faces,
are those who have worked hard and made contributions,
but you reward them last.
Now, having a place among those rewarded last,
my heart cannot overcome its sorrow,
therefore I cry.
Moreover, I have used many deceptions to help you return to your state.
I still despise myself,
how much more should you?"
He bowed twice and resigned.
Wén Gōng (文公) stopped him, saying:
"The proverb says:
'When building an altar,
grab the hoe and place it there,
then wear ceremonial robes and worship it.'
Now you helped me take it,
but will not help me govern it;
you helped me place it,
but will not help me worship it.
How can that be?'"
He untied the left horse of his chariot
and swore an oath by the river.
Bǔ Zǐ (卜子), a man from Zhèng (鄭) County, had his wife make trousers for him.
His wife asked, saying:
"What should the new trousers be like?"
The husband said:
"Like my old trousers."
So the wife tore the new trousers
to make them like the old ones.
A man from Zhèng (鄭) County found a yoke,
but did not know its name,
and asked someone, saying:
"What kind of thing is this?"
The person replied:
"This is a yoke."
Soon after, he found another one.
He asked someone, saying:
"What kind of thing is this?"
The person replied:
"This is a yoke."
The man who asked was furious, saying:
"Before you said it was a yoke,
and now you say it is a yoke,
what is the meaning of this?
You are deceiving me!"
Then he fought with him.
A man of Wèi (衛) was helping with the hunting,
when a bird arrived,
he first waved his sleeve at it,
startling the bird and preventing him from shooting it.
The wife of Bǔ Zǐ (卜子), a man from Zhèng (鄭) County, went to the market,
bought a turtle and returned home.
Passing the Yǐng (潁) River,
thinking that it was thirsty,
she released it to drink,
and then lost her turtle.
When a younger person attends an elder during drinking,
the elder drinks,
and then the younger person drinks too.
It is said that:
A man from Lǔ (魯) was pleased with himself,
seeing an old man drinking wine but unable to finish the cup,
he spat at him,
and also imitated him by spitting.
First:
A young man from Sòng wanting to imitate goodness,
saw an elder drink without leaving any behind,
though he couldn't handle the liquor, he wanted to finish it all.
The *Shū* says:
"Gird it, bind it."
A Sòng man governing,
because of this, wore a heavy belt to bind himself.
People asked:
"What is this for?"
He replied:
"The *Shū* says so;
it is certainly so."
The *Shū* says:
"Having been carved and polished,
return to your original simplicity."
A Liáng man governing,
in his actions and words, imitated learning,
and acted according to the written word,
saying:
"It is difficult."
Ultimately, he lost sight of the substance.
People asked:
"What is this for?"
He replied:
"The *Shū* says so;
it is certainly so."
A man from Yǐng was writing a letter to the Chancellor of Yān.
Writing at night,
the lamp was dim,
so he told the candle-holder:
"Hold the candle up."
In speaking, he wrote the words "hold the candle up."
"Hold the candle up"
was not the meaning of the letter.
The Yān Chancellor received the letter and was pleased with it,
saying: " 'Hold the candle up'
means valuing brightness;
to value brightness
is to promote the worthy and appoint them."
The Yān Chancellor reported this to the king.
The king was greatly pleased,
and the state was well-governed.
Well-governed it was,
but not according to the meaning of the letter.
Scholars of today who follow this example are numerous.
A man from Zhèng was about to buy shoes.
First, he measured his feet and placed the measurement on his seat.
He went to the market but forgot to take the measurement.
Having obtained the shoes,
he then said:
"I forgot to bring the measurement."
He returned to get it.
By the time he returned,
the market was over,
and he could not get the shoes.
Someone asked:
"Why didn't you try them on your feet?"
He said:
"I would rather trust the measurement
than trust myself."
Discourse Four:
Wáng Dēng became the magistrate of Zhōngmóu,
and reported to Lord Xiāng of Jìn, saying:
"In Zhōngmóu there are gentlemen named Zhōng Zhāng and Xū Jǐ,
who cultivate themselves greatly,
and whose learning is very broad.
Why doesn't your lordship promote them?"
The lord said:
"If you see them,
I will make them senior grand masters."
The chief minister advised, saying:
"Senior grand master is a high rank in Jìn.
To receive it without merit
is not the will of the Jìn ministers.
Has your lordship only heard of it and not seen it?"
Lord Xiāng said:
"I value Dēng;
I have both heard of him and seen him.
Those whom Dēng values,
I will also hear of and see.
It is impossible to only hear and see one's self."
Wáng Dēng in one day saw two senior grand masters,
and granted them fields and houses.
The people of Zhōngmóu abandoned their field work,
sold their houses and gardens to follow scholars.
Half the district did so.
Shū Xiàng was driving the chariot.
Lord Píng requested an audience,
the lord's calf cramped, his foot went numb, and his muscles spasmed,
but he did not dare to move from his seat.
The state of Jìn heard of it, and all said:
"Shū Xiàng is a worthy man;
Lord Píng respects him.
He cramped and dared not move from his seat."
Those in the state of Jìn who resigned to emulate Shū Xiàng
were the mainstay of the state.
A man from Zhèng County named Qū Gōng,
hearing of the enemy,
was afraid,
and therefore died;
after his fear,
he came back to life.
Lord Zhào Fù had Lǐ Cī observe
whether Zhōngshān could be attacked.
He returned and reported:
"Zhōngshān can be attacked.
If your lordship does not attack quickly,
Qí and Yān will be next."
Lord Fù said:
"Why can it be attacked?"
Lǐ Cī replied:
"Its lord admires scholars who live in caves;
he takes off his mat and carriage
to see men in poor alleys and narrow lanes
by the dozens;
he treats commoners with the courtesy due to a worthy
by the hundreds."
The lord said:
"According to your words,
he is a worthy lord;
how can he be attacked?"
Cī said: "That is not so.
If one honors scholars who live in caves
and gives them audience in court,
then soldiers will be lazy in battle formation;
if the ruler honors scholars,
and scholars live in court,
then farmers will be lazy in the fields.
If soldiers are lazy in battle formation,
then the army will be weak;
if farmers are lazy in the fields,
then the state will be poor.
If the army is weaker than the enemy
and the state is poor internally,
and it does not perish,
that has never happened.
Is it not right to attack?"
Lord Fù said:
"Good."
He raised an army and attacked Zhōngshān,
and thus destroyed it.
Discourse Five:
Duke Huán of Qí liked to wear purple,
and the whole country wore purple.
At that time,
five bolts of undyed silk could not buy one bolt of purple.
Duke Huán was troubled by this,
and said to Guǎn Zhòng:
"I like to wear purple,
and purple is very expensive.
The people of the country like to wear purple without stopping,
what should I do?"
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"If you want to stop it,
why don't you try not wearing purple yourself?"
He told his attendants:
"I hate the smell of purple very much."
Therefore, when any attendants came forward wearing purple,
the duke would always say:
"Stand back,
I hate the smell of purple."
The duke said:
"Alright."
On that day,
none of the courtiers wore purple;
the next day,
none of the people in the country wore purple;
after three days,
no one within the borders wore purple.
The first says:
The king of Qí 齊王 was fond of wearing purple,
and the people of Qí 齊 also became fond of it.
In the state of Qí 齊, five plain colors could not be exchanged for one purple.
The king of Qí 齊 worried about the high price of purple.
Fù Yuè 傅說 said to the king,
"The *Shī* 詩 says:
'If you do not do it yourself, if you are not involved personally,
the common people will not believe you.'
Now, if Your Majesty wishes the people not to wear purple,
Your Majesty, please take off your purple robe and attend court.
If any of the court officials advances wearing purple,
say:
'Stay far away!
I detest the smell.'"
On that day,
none of the gentlemen-in-waiting wore purple;
in that month,
none in the state wore purple;
in that year,
none within the borders wore purple.
Zhèng Jiǎn Gōng 鄭簡公 said to Zǐchǎn 子產,
"Our state is small,
squeezed between Jīng 荊 and Jìn 晉.
Now the city walls are not complete,
and the armor is not prepared,
so we cannot be ready for the unexpected."
Zǐchǎn 子產 said,
"I have already made its exterior distant,
and have made its interior secure.
Although the state is small,
it is still not in danger.
Your Lordship, do not worry about it."
Therefore, there was no trouble during Jiǎn Gōng's 簡公 lifetime.
The first says:
Zǐchǎn 子產 was the prime minister of Zhèng 鄭.
Jiǎn Gōng 簡公 said to Zǐchǎn 子產,
"Drinking wine is not enjoyable.
The sacrificial vessels are not large enough,
the bells, drums, *yú* 竽 and *sè* 瑟 are not sounding,
my affairs are not unified;
the state is not stable,
the people are not well-governed,
and cultivation and warfare are not in harmony.
This is also your fault.
You have your duty,
and I also have my duty,
let each of us guard our duty."
Zǐchǎn 子產 withdrew and implemented his policies for five years.
There were no thieves in the state,
no one picked up lost items on the road,
and no one reached for peaches and dates that cast shade on the street;
a needle or knife lost on the road could be found in three days.
If this was not changed for three years,
the people would not go hungry.
Sòng Xiāng Gōng 宋襄公 fought with the people of Chǔ 楚
on Zhuō Gǔ 涿谷.
The people of Sòng 宋 had already formed their ranks,
but the people of Chǔ 楚 had not yet crossed the river.
The Right Sīmǎ 司馬, Gōu Qiáng 購強, hurried forward and advised,
"The people of Chǔ 楚 are many, and the people of Sòng 宋 are few.
Please allow the people of Chǔ 楚 to cross halfway, and strike them before they have formed ranks,
and we will surely defeat them."
Xiāng Gōng 襄公 said,
"I have heard that a gentleman says:
'Do not inflict a second wound,
do not capture the gray-haired,
do not push people into danger,
do not corner people in distress,
do not strike an unformed line.'
Now, if we were to strike them before they have crossed,
it would harm righteousness.
Please allow the people of Chǔ 楚 to completely cross and form their ranks
and then we will beat the drums and advance our soldiers."
The Right Sīmǎ 司馬 said,
"Your Lordship does not love the people of Sòng 宋,
your inner thoughts are incomplete,
and you are only doing it for righteousness."
The Duke said,
"Do not break ranks, and carry out the law."
The Right Sīmǎ 司馬 returned to the ranks,
and the people of Chǔ 楚 had already formed ranks and prepared their formations.
Only then did the Duke beat the drums.
The people of Sòng 宋 were utterly defeated,
and the Duke was wounded in the thigh.
He died after three days.
This was the disaster of admiring and personally pursuing benevolence and righteousness.
If one must rely on the ruler personally doing everything
before the people listen and follow,
then it will lead the ruler
to plow to get food,
and to serve in battle in a file formation.
Only then would the people be willing to plow and fight.
Wouldn't the ruler be in great danger?
And wouldn't the ministers be very secure?
Qí Jǐng Gōng 齊景公 was visiting Shào Hǎi 少海,
and a messenger on horseback came from the middle of the group to announce,
"Yīng 嬰 is very ill,
and about to die,
I fear that Your Lordship will be too late."
Jǐng Gōng 景公 immediately rose,
and another messenger on horseback arrived.
Jǐng Gōng 景公 said,
"Quickly harness the carriage of Fán Qiě 煩且,
and have the groom Zōu Zǐ 騶子 and Hán Shū 韓樞 drive it."
After traveling several hundred steps,
he thought that Zōu 騶 was not fast enough,
so he snatched the reins and drove himself;
after several hundred more steps,
he thought that the horses were not advancing quickly enough,
so he completely abandoned the carriage and ran.
With the excellence of Fán Qiě 煩且
and the skill of Zōu Zǐ 騶子 and Hán Shū 韓樞,
he thought that it was not as good as running himself.
Wèi Zhāo Wáng 魏昭王 wanted
to participate in official affairs,
and said to Mèngcháng Jūn 孟嘗君,
"I want to participate in official affairs."
Mèngcháng Jūn 孟嘗君 said,
"If Your Majesty wants to participate in official affairs,
then why not try practicing reading the law?"
Zhāo Wáng 昭王 read the law for more than ten slips and then fell asleep.
The king said,
"I cannot read this law."
If you do not personally grasp the power and authority,
but want to do what ministers should do,
isn't sleeping appropriate?
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said,
"For a ruler,
it is like a basin;
the people
are like water.
If the basin is square, the water is square;
if the basin is round, the water is round."
The ruler of Zōu 鄒 was fond of wearing long tassels,
and those around him all wore long tassels,
so tassels became very expensive.
The ruler of Zōu 鄒 was worried about this,
and asked those around him.
Those around him said,
"Because Your Lordship is fond of wearing them,
the people also wear them a lot,
and that is why they are expensive."
The ruler then cut off his own tassel and went out,
and no one in the state wore long tassels.
The ruler could not issue an order
to regulate the clothing of the people to prohibit it,
but instead cut off his tassel to show the people first,
which is like first inflicting punishment to govern the people.
Shū Xiàng 叔向 was distributing the spoils of the hunt.
Those who had done more work received more,
and those who had done less work received less.
Hán Zhāo Hóu 韓昭侯 said to Shēn Zǐ 申子,
"The laws and standards are very difficult to implement."
Shēn Zǐ 申子 said,
"The law is
to grant rewards based on merit
and to assign offices based on ability.
Now Your Lordship establishes laws and standards,
but listens to the requests of those around you,
which is why it is difficult to implement."
Zhāo Hóu 昭侯 said,
"From now on, I know how to implement the law.
What shall I listen to?"
One day,
Shēn Zǐ 申子 requested an official position for his elder cousin.
Zhāo Hóu 昭侯 said,
"This is not what I learned from you.
If I listen to your request,
would I be ruining your principles?
Would I be abandoning the use of your request?"
Shēn Zǐ 申子 withdrew and requested punishment.
Discourse Six: 〓#
Jìn Wén Gōng 晉文公 attacked Yuán 原,
taking ten days' worth of provisions,
and thus set a ten-day deadline with his senior officials.
After ten days, Yuán 原 had not fallen,
so he struck the metal and retreated,
calling off the troops and departing.
A scholar came from Yuán.
He said, "Yuán will surrender in three days."
The courtiers and attendants advised,
"Yuán's food is exhausted, and their strength is depleted.
Your Lordship, please wait for them."
The Duke said,
"I promised the scholar ten days.
If I don't leave
it will be a loss of my credibility.
Gaining Yuán but losing credibility
I will not do."
Thereupon, he withdrew his troops and left.
The people of Yuán heard of it and said,
"Having a ruler so trustworthy,
how can we not submit?"
So they surrendered to the Duke.
The people of Wèi heard of it and said,
"Having a ruler so trustworthy,
how can we not follow him?"
So they surrendered to the Duke.
Kǒngzǐ heard of it and recorded it, saying,
"Conquering Yuán and gaining Wèi was due to trustworthiness."
Duke Wén asked Jī Zhèng,
"How to relieve famine?"
He replied,
"Trustworthiness."
The Duke said,
"How to establish trustworthiness?"
He said,
"Trust in titles, trust in affairs, trust in righteousness.
If you trust in titles,
then the courtiers will uphold their duties,
good and evil will not overstep their bounds,
and all affairs will not be neglected;
If you trust in affairs,
then you will not miss the opportune time,
and the people will not overstep their bounds;
If you trust in righteousness,
then close relatives will encourage each other,
and those who are far away will submit."
Wú Qǐ went out and met an old friend who stopped him for a meal.
The old friend said,
"Okay,
I will return home and prepare it."
Wú Qǐ said,
"I will wait for you before eating."
The old friend did not come until evening,
and Qǐ did not eat, waiting for him.
Early the next morning,
he sent someone to look for the old friend.
When the old friend came,
he then ate with him.
Marquis Wèi Wén of Wèi made an appointment with a forester for hunting.
The next day,
there was a strong wind,
and his attendants tried to stop Wén Hóu.
He did not listen,
saying,
"No. To lose credibility
due to the wind
I will not do."
So he drove his own chariot and went,
braving the wind to dismiss the forester.
Zēngzǐ's wife went to the market,
and her son followed her, crying.
His mother said,
"You go back,
and when I return, I will kill a pig for you."
When she returned from the market,
Zēngzǐ wanted to catch a pig and kill it.
His wife stopped him, saying,
"I was just playing with the child."
Zēngzǐ said,
"Children should not be trifled with.
Children do not have knowledge of their own,
but learn from their parents,
listening to their parents' teachings.
Now if you deceive him,
you are teaching your child to deceive.
If a mother deceives her child,
and the child does not believe his mother,
it is not a way to cultivate proper education."
So he cooked the pig.
King Lì of Chǔ had an alert
and prepared a drum
to signal the people to defend.
He was drunk with wine
and accidentally beat the drum,
causing the people great alarm.
He sent someone to stop them,
saying,
"I was drunk and playing with my attendants,
and accidentally beat the drum."
The people all dispersed.
After several months,
there was an alert,
and the people did not respond to the drumbeat.
So he changed the order and made a clear announcement,
and the people believed him.
Lǐ Kuī warned his two squads,
saying,
"Be vigilant against the enemy,
they will arrive and attack you morning and evening."
This happened two or three times, but the enemy did not come.
The two squads grew lax
and did not believe Lǐ Kuī.
After several months,
the people of Qín launched a surprise attack,
nearly seizing their army.
This is the disaster of not being trusted.
Another account says:
Lǐ Kuī fought with the people of Qín,
and said to the left squad,
"Advance quickly!
The right squad has already advanced."
Then he rode to the right squad and said,
"The left squad has already advanced."
The left and right squads said,
"We have already advanced."
Thereupon, they all fought to advance.
The following year,
he fought with the people of Qín.
The people of Qín launched a surprise attack,
nearly seizing their army.
This is the disaster of not being trusted.
There were two people who were suing each other.
Zǐchǎn separated them and did not allow them to communicate directly,
but relayed their words to each other, so they understood.
Duke Sì of Wèi had someone falsely pass through the market checkpoint.
The checkpoint guard questioned and challenged him,
so he bribed the checkpoint guard with gold.
The checkpoint guard then let him go.
Duke Sì said to the checkpoint guard,
"At a certain time, a guest passed by and gave you gold,"
and then he reprimanded him.
The checkpoint guard was very frightened,
thinking Duke Sì was wise and discerning.
Classic 1:
If one is punished for a crime,
people will not resent their superiors.
(For example,) Què Wēi sat upright before Zǐgāo.
If one is rewarded for merit,
the subject will not be grateful to their ruler.
(For example,) Dí Huáng held the right tally and rode in a carriage.
If King Xiāng did not understand this,
then Zhāo Mǎo would wear straw sandals despite having five carriages.
If the ruler does not exceed their responsibilities,
the subject will not falsely claim ability.
Then the subject will become Fū Shàoshì Zhōu.
Classic 2:
Relying on power and not on trustworthiness
is why Dōngguō Yá criticized Guǎn Zhòng.
Relying on tactics and not on trustworthiness
is why Hún Xuān criticized Duke Wén.
Therefore, a ruler who has tactics
must reward based on trust to fully utilize abilities
and punish strictly to prohibit evil.
Even if there are conflicting actions,
one will surely obtain benefit.
When Jiǎn Zhǔ was the prime minister of Yáng Hǔ,
Duke Āi asked about "one foot".
Classic 3:
If the principles of ruler and subject are lost,
then King Wén will personally carry and take pride.
If the places for court and leisure are not distinguished,
then Jì Sūn will be solemn his entire life and encounter assassins.
Classic 4:
If you benefit what you prohibit
and prohibit what you benefit,
even a god cannot succeed.
If you praise what you condemn
and condemn what you praise,
even Yáo cannot govern well.
To make a door but not allow entry,
to entrust benefit but not allow advancement,
is how chaos is produced.
If the Marquis of Qí (齊侯) did not listen to his attendants,
the Lord of Wèi (魏主) did not listen to flatterers,
and thereby clearly observed his ministers,
then even great matters would not waste gold and money,
and the incompetent would not be able to use jade.
Sīmǎ Bào's (西門豹) request to return and govern Yè (鄴)
is sufficient to know this.
It is like stealing an infant's fine fur coat,
and giving Róng (榮) clothing to a person with mutilated feet, a dangerous son.
If Zǐ Chuò (子綽) had attendants drawing on both sides,
chasing away ants and flies,
how could he avoid the worries of Duke Huán (桓公) when he sought an official,
and the concerns of Lord Xuān (宣主) about lean horses?
Chapter Five: 〓#
If a minister takes humility and frugality as his conduct,
then rank is not enough to show appreciation;
if favor and glory are without restraint,
then ministers will encroach and oppress.
The explanation lies in Miáo Bēn Huáng (苗賁皇) not offering Bá (伯),
and Confucius' criticism of Yàn Yīng (晏嬰).
Therefore, Zhòng Ní (仲尼) discussed Guǎn Zhòng (管仲) and Sūn Shū'áo (孫叔敖).
And when the appearance of those entering and exiting changes,
Yáng Hǔ's (陽虎) words reveal his ministers.
And the way Lord Jiǎn (簡主) responds to his ministers loses the art of a ruler.
If cliques harmonize with each other,
and ministers get what they want,
then the ruler is isolated;
if ministers are publicly recommended,
and those below do not agree with each other,
then the ruler is enlightened.
If Yáng Hǔ (陽虎) had the virtue of Zhào Wǔ (趙武)
and the fairness of Xiè Hú (解狐),
Lord Jiǎn (簡主) would have regarded him as thorns,
which is not the way to teach the state.
Chapter Six: 〓#
If the ducal house is humbled,
then direct speech is resented;
if private conduct prevails,
then public achievements are few.
The explanation lies in Wén Zǐ's (文子) direct speech,
Wǔ Zǐ's (武子) use of a staff;
Zǐ Chǎn's (子產) loyal remonstrance,
Zǐ Guó's (子國) scolding anger;
Liáng Chē's (梁車) use of law,
and Lord Chéng (成侯) collecting the seals;
Guǎn Zhòng's (管仲) public-mindedness,
and the people's slander and resentment.
Explanation One: 〓#
When Confucius was a minister in Wèi (衛),
his disciple Zǐ Gāo (子皋) was a prison official,
and he mutilated a person's foot,
and the mutilated person guarded the gate.
Someone spoke ill of Confucius to the Lord of Wèi (衛君),
saying:
"Ní (尼) wants to rebel."
The Lord of Wèi (衛君) wanted to arrest Confucius.
Confucius fled,
and his disciples all escaped.
Zǐ Gāo (子皋) followed him out the door,
and the mutilated person pulled him
and hid him in a room under the gate,
and the officers could not find him.
At midnight,
Zǐ Gāo (子皋) asked the mutilated person:
"I could not violate the lord's laws
and personally mutilate your foot,
this is the time for you to take revenge,
and why are you willing to help me escape?
How did I get this from you?"
The mutilated person said:
"My foot was cut off,
it is certainly my fault that I deserve it,
there is nothing that can be done about it.
But when you, sir, governed the prison and judged me,
you leaned towards the laws,
and repeatedly spoke to me with words,
you greatly desired my acquittal,
and I knew it.
When the prison decided and the crime was determined,
you were apprehensive and displeased,
which showed in your face,
and I saw it and knew it again.
It was not just for me privately,
but because the nature of benevolence
is inherently so.
This is why I am pleased
and grateful to you, sir."
Confucius said:
"Those who are good at creating benefits
cultivate virtue,
those who are not good at creating benefits
cultivate resentment.
The gài (概)
is what levels measurements,
the official
is what levels the law,
those who govern the state
must not lose balance."
Tián Zǐfāng (田子方) went from Qí (齊) to Wèi (魏),
and saw Dí Huáng (翟黃) riding in a carriage with harnessed horses.
Fāng (方) thought it was Lord Wén (文侯),
so he moved his carriage to a different road to avoid him,
but it was just Dí Huáng (翟黃).
Fāng (方) asked:
"Why are you riding in this carriage?"
He said:
"The lord planned to attack Zhōngshān (中山),
and I recommended Dí Jiǎo (翟角),
and the plan was successful;
and when he attacked it,
I recommended Yuè Yáng (樂羊), and Zhōngshān (中山) was captured;
after capturing Zhōngshān (中山),
he was worried about governing it,
and I recommended Lǐ Kè (李克), and Zhōngshān (中山) was governed:
therefore, the lord bestowed this carriage."
Fāng (方) said:
"The reward for the achievement is still small."
When Qín (秦) and Hán (韓) attacked Wèi (魏),
Zhāo Mǎo (昭卯) persuaded them to the west, and Qín (秦) and Hán (韓) stopped;
when Qí (齊) and Jīng (荊) attacked Wèi (魏),
Mǎo (卯) persuaded them to the east, and Qí (齊) and Jīng (荊) stopped.
King Xiāng of Wèi (魏襄王) supported him with five chariots.
Mǎo (卯) said:
"Bó Yí (伯夷) was buried as a general at the foot of Mount Shǒuyáng (首陽山),
and the world said:
'Since Bó Yí (伯夷) was virtuous
and known for his benevolence,
to bury him as a general,
is like not covering his hands and feet.'
Now I have stopped the armies of four states,
and the king has given me five chariots,
this reward for the achievement
is like a cripple winning and wearing shoes."
"Shào Shì Zhōu (少室周) was a man of ancient integrity, honesty, purity, and sincerity,
and he was a strongman for Lord Xiāng of Zhào (趙襄主).
He wrestled with Xú Zǐjiǎo of Zhōngmù (中牟徐子角),
and was not as good as him,
so he entered and told Lord Xiāng (襄主)
that he would replace himself.
Lord Xiāng (襄主) said:
"Your position
is what people desire,
why are you recommending Xú Zǐ (徐子) to replace yourself?"
He said:
"I serve the lord with strength.
Now Xú Zǐ's (徐子) strength is greater than mine,
if I don't recommend him to replace myself,
I'm afraid someone else will say it
and I will be guilty."
Another account says:
Shào Shì Zhōu (少室周) was Lord Xiāng's (襄主) chariot driver,
and when they arrived at Jìnyáng (晉陽),
there was a strongman named Niú Zǐgēng (牛子耕),
who wrestled with him and did not win.
Zhōu (周) said to the lord:
"The reason why you have me drive the chariot
is because I am strong.
Now there is someone stronger than me,
I wish to recommend him."
Explanation Two: 〓#
When Duke Huán of Qí (齊桓公) was about to appoint Guǎn Zhòng (管仲),
he ordered his ministers:
"I am going to appoint Guǎn Zhòng (管仲) as my second father.
Those who approve, enter the gate and go to the left,
those who disapprove, enter the gate and go to the right."
Dōngguō Yá (東郭牙) stood in the middle of the gate.
The Duke said:
"I appointed Guǎn Zhòng as Zhòng Fù,
and issued an order saying:
'The worthy stand to the left,
and the unworthy to the right.'
Why do you stand in the middle of the gate?"
Yá replied:
"With Guǎn Zhòng's wisdom,
is he capable of scheming for the world?"
The Duke said:
"He is."
"With his decisiveness,
is he bold enough to carry out great affairs?"
The Duke said:
"He is."
Yá said:
"If you know he is capable of scheming for the world
and decisive enough to carry out great affairs,
then you should entrust him with the power of the state.
With Guǎn Zhòng's abilities,
taking advantage of your position to govern the state of Qí,
how could there not be danger?"
The Duke said:
"Good."
Then he ordered Xí Péng to manage internal affairs and
Guǎn Zhòng to manage external affairs, so they could assist each other.
When Duke Wén of Jìn fled,
Jī Zhèng carried a wine pot and food
and followed him.
They got lost and lost their way,
and he became separated from the Duke.
He was hungry and wept on the road,
staying hungry and daring not to eat.
When Duke Wén returned to the country,
he raised an army to attack Yuán,
and conquered and captured it.
Duke Wén said:
"He lightly endured the suffering of hunger
and was determined to protect the wine pot and food;
he will certainly not betray Yuán."
Therefore, he appointed him as the magistrate of Yuán.
The senior official Hún Xuān heard of this and criticized it,
saying:
"To rely on the fact that he didn't move the wine pot and food
and presume he won't betray Yuán,
isn't that lacking in method?"
Therefore, a wise ruler
does not rely on others not betraying him,
but relies on his own inability to be betrayed;
he does not rely on others not deceiving him,
but relies on his own inability to be deceived.
Yáng Hǔ advised:
"If the ruler is wise and enlightened,
then wholeheartedly serve him;
if he is unworthy,
then embellish wickedness and test him."
He was driven out of Lǔ,
suspected in Qí,
and fled to Zhào.
Lord Jiǎn of Zhào welcomed him and made him his minister.
His attendants said:
"Hǔ is good at stealing the government of other states,
why do you make him a minister?"
Lord Jiǎn said:
"Yáng Hǔ is intent on seizing,
and I am intent on guarding."
Therefore, he held to his methods and controlled him.
Yáng Hǔ dared not do wrong,
and diligently served Lord Jiǎn,
strengthening his lord's power,
almost to the point of hegemony.
Duke Āi of Lǔ asked Kǒngzǐ:
"I have heard that in ancient times there was Kuí with one foot.
Is it really true that he had one foot?"
Kǒngzǐ replied:
"No,
Kuí did not have one foot.
Kuí was full of anger and wickedness,
and many people did not like him.
However,
the reason he was able to escape harm from others
was because of his trustworthiness.
People all said:
'This one thing alone
is enough.'
Kuí did not have one foot,
but one quality was enough."
Duke Āi said:
"If it is truly like that,
then one is indeed enough."
Another account says:
Duke Āi asked Kǒngzǐ:
"I have heard that Kuí had one foot,
is it true?"
He said:
"Kuí
was a man,
why would he have one foot?
He had no other special qualities,
but was uniquely skilled in music.
Yáo said:
'Kuí, with this one quality, is enough.'
and made him director of music.
Therefore, the gentleman said:
Kuí had one
*zú* 足,
not one foot 足."
Explanation Three:
When King Wén attacked Chóng,
he arrived at the mound of Fèng Huáng,
and the tie of his socks came undone.
He then tied it himself.
Tài Gōng Wàng said:
"Why do you do this?"
The King said:
"A superior
ruler treats those who live with him
all as his teachers;
a middling
ruler treats them all as his friends;
an inferior
ruler treats them all as his servants.
Now, they are all ministers of the former ruler,
so there is no one I can employ."
Another account says:
When Duke Wén of Jìn fought with Chǔ,
he arrived at the tomb of Huáng Fèng,
and the tie of his shoe came undone.
He then tied it himself.
His attendants said:
"Couldn't you have someone do it for you?"
The Duke said:
"I have heard:
A superior
ruler treats those he lives with
all as those he fears;
a middling
ruler treats those he lives with
all as those he loves;
an inferior
ruler treats those he lives with
all as those he insults.
Although I am unworthy,
the people of the former ruler are all present,
and that is why I find it difficult."
Jì Sūn loved scholars
and was always solemn.
His residence and clothing were always as if he were at court.
But Jì Sūn was actually lazy
and had faults,
and could not maintain it for long.
Therefore, the guests thought he was tired of them and looked down on them.
They resented him together
and then killed Jì Sūn.
Therefore, the gentleman avoids excess and extremes.
Another account says:
Nángōng Jìngzǐ asked Yán Zhuōjù:
"Jì Sūn supported the followers of Kǒngzǐ,
those who wore court attire and sat with him numbered in the tens,
yet he encountered an assassin,
why?"
He said:
"In the past, King Chéng of Zhōu
kept close to jesters and dwarfs
to satisfy his desires,
but decided matters with gentlemen,
and was thus able to fulfill his desires in the world.
Now, Jì Sūn supported the followers of Kǒngzǐ,
those who wore court attire and sat with him numbered in the tens,
but decided matters with jesters and dwarfs,
and therefore encountered an assassin.
Therefore, it is said:
It is not about who you live with,
but about who you consult with."
Kǒngzǐ was seated beside Lǔ Āigōng,
and Āigōng presented him with peaches and millet.
Āigōng said:
"Please, use them."
Zhòngní first ate the millet and then tasted the peach,
and those around him covered their mouths and laughed.
Āigōng said:
"Millet
is not for eating,
but for cleansing the peach."
Zhòngní replied:
"Qiū understands.
Millet
is the chief of the five grains,
used as the primary offering when sacrificing to former kings.
Fruits and gourds are six in number,
but the peach is the lowest,
and may not enter the ancestral temple when sacrificing to former kings.
What Qiū has heard is that
a gentleman uses the base to cleanse the noble,
but has not heard of using the noble to cleanse the base.
Now to use the chief of the five grains
to cleanse the lowest of fruits and gourds,
this is using the superior to cleanse the inferior.
Qiū believes this hinders righteousness,
so I dared not put it before
the offerings to the ancestral temple."
Jiǎn Zhǔ said to his attendants:
"The carriage mat is too beautiful.
Though a hat may be cheap,
one must wear it on the head;
though shoes may be expensive,
one must wear them on the feet.
Now that the carriage mat is like this,
too beautiful,
with what kind of rough shoes shall I tread upon it?
To beautify the bottom and deplete the top
is the root of hindering righteousness."
Fèi Zhòng persuaded Zhòu, saying:
"Xībó Chāng is virtuous,
the people are pleased with him,
the feudal lords are attached to him,
he must be executed;
if he is not executed,
he will surely become a disaster for Yīn."
Zhòu said:
"Your words concern a man of righteousness;
why should he be executed?"
Fèi Zhòng said:
"Even if a hat is worn and tattered,
it must be worn on the head;
even if shoes are five-colored,
they must be trod upon the ground.
Now Xībó Chāng,
a subject,
cultivates righteousness and the people turn to him;
in the end, he will become a worry for the world;
will he surely prosper?
If a subject does not use his virtue for his lord, 〓#
he cannot but be executed. 〓#
Moreover, for a lord to execute a subject,
what fault is there?"
Zhòu said:
"仁rényì, benevolence and righteousness,
is what superiors use to encourage inferiors.
Now Chāng loves 仁rényì,
it is not permissible to execute him."
His three attempts at persuasion were not heeded,
therefore he perished.
Qí Xuānwáng asked Kuāng Qiàn:
"Are Confucian scholars gamblers?"
He said:
"No."
The king said:
"Why?"
Kuāng Qiàn replied:
"Gambling values the owl;
the winner must kill the owl.
To kill the owl
is to kill what is valued.
Confucian scholars consider it harmful to righteousness,
therefore they do not gamble."
He asked again:
"Do Confucian scholars shoot birds with arrows attached to strings?"
He said:
"No.
Shooting with arrows attached to strings
is harming the superior from below,
it is injuring the ruler from below.
Confucian scholars consider it harmful to righteousness,
therefore they do not shoot with arrows attached to strings."
He asked again:
"Do Confucian scholars play the zither?"
He said: "No.
The zither uses the small strings to make a large sound,
and the large strings to make a small sound,
thus small and large are reversed in order,
and noble and base are transposed.
Confucian scholars consider it harmful to righteousness,
therefore they do not play it."
Xuānwáng said:
"Good."
Zhòngní said:
"Rather than having the people flatter those below,
it is better to have the people flatter those above."
Discourses Four: 〓#
Jù was a recluse of Qí;
Chán was a recluse of Wèi.
The rulers of Qí and Wèi were unenlightened,
unable to personally oversee their territories,
and listened to the words of those around them,
therefore these two men spent gold and jade
seeking official positions.
Xīmén Bào, as magistrate of Yè,
was pure, diligent, honest, and sincere,
with no private interests even to the tip of an autumn hair.
But he greatly alienated those around him.
Those around him therefore colluded and slandered him.
After a year,
during the annual report,
the ruler took back his seal.
Bào requested himself, saying:
"Formerly, your subject did not know how to govern Yè,
but now your subject understands;
I wish to request the seal
to govern Yè again.
If I do not succeed,
I will submit to the punishment of the axe and block."
Wénhóu could not bear it
and returned it to him.
Bào then heavily taxed the people
and eagerly served those around him.
After a year,
during the annual report,
Wénhóu welcomed and bowed to him.
Bào replied:
"Last year, your subject governed Yè for you,
and you took your subject's seal;
now your subject governs Yè for those around you,
and you bow to your subject.
Your subject cannot govern."
He then submitted the seal and left.
Wénhóu did not accept it,
saying:
"Formerly, I did not understand you,
now I understand.
I wish you would strive to govern it for me."
He then did not accept.
In Qí, there was the son of a dog thief
who joked and boasted with the son of a crippled man.
The thief's son said:
"My father's fur coat is the only one with a tail."
The crippled man's son said:
"My father is the only one who doesn't lose his trousers in winter."
Zǐ Chuò said:
"No one can draw a square with their left hand
and a circle with their right hand at the same time.
Using meat to get rid of ants only increases their number;
using fish to drive away flies only attracts more."
Húangōng said to Guǎn Zhòng:
"There are few official positions but many seeking them,
I am worried about it."
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"If you do not listen to the requests of those around you,
grant emoluments based on ability,
and bestow offices based on recorded merit,
then no one will dare to seek office;
what do you have to worry about?"
Hán Xuānzi said:
"My horses have plenty of beans and millet,
but they are very thin.
Why is this?
I am worried about it."
Zhōu Shì replied:
"Even if you order the stablemen to feed them entirely with millet,
it is impossible for them to not be thin.
It cannot be achieved.
In name, it is said that they are given plenty,
but in reality, it is little;
even if you try to prevent them from becoming thin,
it cannot be achieved either.
If the master does not examine the true situation,
and just sits and worries about it,
the horses still won't get fat."
Huán Gōng asked Guǎn Zhòng about appointing officials.
Guǎn Zhòng said:
"To be discerning in words,
and incorruptible in handling goods,
familiar with human nature,
I, Yí Wú, am not as good as Xián Shāng.
Please appoint him as the chief judge.
In ascending and descending, being respectful and yielding,
in demonstrating ritual and treating guests,
I am not as good as Xí Péng.
Please appoint him as the grand master of ceremonies.
In reclaiming overgrown land,
opening up land to produce grain,
I am not as good as Níng Qī.
Please appoint him as the grand minister of agriculture.
Once the three armies are formed into battle array,
to make the soldiers regard death as returning home,
I am not as good as Gōngzǐ Chéngfǔ.
Please appoint him as the grand commander.
In directly remonstrating with strong words,
I am not as good as Dōngguō Yá.
Please appoint him as a remonstrating minister.
To govern Qí,
these five men are sufficient;
if you want to become a hegemon or a king,
then Yí Wú is here."
Saying Five: 〓#
When Mèng Xiànbo was the prime minister of Jìn,
purslane and goosefoot grew under the hall,
and brambles grew outside the gate.
He did not eat two kinds of delicacies,
nor did he sit on layered mats.
Jìn had no concubines wearing silk,
nor did he feed his horses with grain,
nor did he go out with carriages.
Shū Xiàng heard of this
and told Miáo Bēnhuáng.
Bēnhuáng criticized him, saying:
"This is taking the ruler's rank and salary
to ingratiate himself with the people below."
One says:
When Mèng Xiànbo was appointed senior minister,
Shū Xiàng went to congratulate him,
but there were guards at the gate,
and the horses did not eat grain.
Xiàng said:
"Why do you not have two horses and two carriages?"
Xiànbo said:
"I observe that the people of the state
still have a hungry look,
therefore I do not feed my horses grain;
many of the gray-haired ones walk on foot,
so I do not have two carriages."
Xiàng said:
"I originally came to congratulate you on becoming a minister,
now I congratulate you on your frugality." 〓#
Xiàng went out, 〓#
and said to Miáo Bēnhuáng: 〓#
"Help me congratulate Xiànbo on his frugality."
Miáozi said:
"What is there to congratulate?
Rank, salary, flags, and emblems
are for distinguishing meritorious achievements
and differentiating the worthy from the unworthy.
Therefore, the laws of the Jìn state
stipulate that senior grandees have two carriages and two teams of horses,
middle grandees have two carriages and one team of horses,
and junior grandees have one team of horses exclusively;
this clarifies the hierarchy.
Moreover, ministers must have military duties,
therefore they repair carriages and horses,
and prepare soldiers and chariots,
to prepare for military affairs.
In times of trouble,
they are prepared for the unexpected;
in times of peace,
they provide for court affairs.
Now, he is disrupting the administration of the Jìn state,
neglecting preparations for the unexpected,
to achieve a reputation for frugality,
and to purify his personal name.
Is Xiànbo's frugality acceptable?
What is there to congratulate?"
When Guǎn Zhòng was prime minister of Qí,
he said:
"I am noble,
yet I am poor."
Huán Gōng said:
"I will give you a family with three estates."
He said:
"I am rich,
yet I am lowly."
Huán Gōng had him stand above Gāo and Guó.
He said:
"I am honored,
yet I am alienated."
So he was made Second Father.
Confucius heard of this and criticized it, saying:
"Extravagance forces pressure on superiors."
One says:
When Guǎn Zhòngfù went out,
he had a vermillion canopy and blue-clad attendants,
and placed drums to announce his return,
his courtyard had displayed tripods,
and his family had three estates.
Confucius said:
"He is a good grandee,
but his extravagance forces pressure on superiors."
When Sūn Shū'áo was prime minister of Chǔ,
he used a rough cart and a female horse,
ate coarse rice and vegetable soup,
had dried fish for meals,
wore lambskin in winter,
and linen clothes in summer.
If his face showed signs of hunger,
then he was a good grandee,
but his frugality forced pressure on those below.
Yáng Hǔ left Qí and fled to Zhào.
Jiǎn Zhǔ asked him, saying:
"I heard that you are good at cultivating people."
Hǔ said:
"When I lived in Lǔ,
I cultivated three men,
and all became magistrates;
when I was accused of crimes in Lǔ,
they all searched for me.
When I lived in Qí,
I recommended three men,
one was able to get close to the king,
one became a county magistrate,
and one became a border patrolman;
when I was accused of crimes,
the one close to the king did not see me,
the county magistrate welcomed me and bound me,
and the border patrolman chased me to the border,
stopping just short of catching me.
I am not good at cultivating people."
The ruler lowered his head and smiled, saying:
"Those who plant mandarin oranges,
when eaten, taste sweet,
and when smelled, are fragrant;
those who plant thorny jujubes,
when grown, prick people.
Therefore, the superior man is careful about what he cultivates."
There was no magistrate in Zhōngmù,
so Jìn Pínggōng asked Zhào Wǔ, saying:
"Zhōngmù
is the thigh and arm of our state,
and the shoulder and thigh of Hándān.
I want to find a good magistrate for it.
Whom should I send?"
Wǔ said:
"Xíng Bózǐ is suitable."
The duke said:
"Is he not your enemy?"
It is said:
"Private vengeance should not enter the public gate."
The duke further asked:
"The head of the central treasury,
whom should I appoint?"
He replied:
"A subject is acceptable."
Therefore, it is said:
"In external appointments, do not avoid enemies;
in internal appointments, do not avoid sons."
Zhào Wǔ recommended forty-six people,
and after Wǔ died,
each took up their positions,
demonstrating his lack of personal bias in this matter.
Píng Gōng asked Shū Xiàng,
"Among the ministers, who is virtuous?"
He replied: "Zhào Wǔ."
The duke said:
"You are biased towards your teacher."
Xiàng said:
"Wǔ stands as if he cannot bear the weight of his clothes,
speaks as if the words are not coming out of his mouth,
yet he has recommended dozens of men,
all of whom have achieved their ambitions,
and the ducal house greatly relies on them.
When Wǔzǐ was alive,
he did not benefit his family;
in death, he did not entrust his orphaned children to anyone.
I dare to consider him virtuous."
Jiě Hú recommended his enemy to Jiǎn Zhǔ to be prime minister.
His enemy thought he would be pardoned by chance,
and so he went to pay his respects and express his gratitude.
Hú then drew his bow and shot at him,
saying:
"My recommendation of you
was a public matter,
because you are capable of the position.
My enmity towards you
is my private grievance,
and I will not, because of my private grievance against you,
suppress you before my ruler."
Therefore, private grievances should not enter the public gate.
It is also said:
Jiě Hú recommended Xíng Bólǔ as the governor of Shàngdǎng.
Lǔ went to thank him, saying:
"You have released me from my crime;
how dare I not bow twice?"
Hú said: "My recommendation of you
was a public matter;
my resentment of you
is a private matter.
Go now;
my resentment of you is as it was before."
A man from Zhèng County was selling piglets,
and someone asked him the price.
He said:
"The road is long, and the day is late;
how can I have time to talk to you?"
Discourse Six:〓#
Fàn Wénzǐ liked direct speech,
and Wǔzǐ struck him with a staff:
"Those who speak directly
are not tolerated by others;
if they are not tolerated,
they endanger themselves.
Not only do they endanger themselves,
but they will also endanger their father."
Zǐchǎn
was the son of Zǐ Guó.
Zǐchǎn was loyal to the ruler of Zhèng,
and Zǐ Guó scolded him, saying:
"To be different from other ministers
and solely loyal to the ruler:
if the ruler is virtuous and wise,
he will listen to you;
if he is not wise,
he will not listen to you.
Whether he listens or not is uncertain,
and you have already separated yourself from the other ministers.
If you are separated from the other ministers,
you will surely endanger yourself.
Not only will you endanger yourself,
but you will also endanger your father."
Liáng Chē had just become the magistrate of Yè,
and his elder sister went to visit him.
It was late in the evening,
and the city gates were closed,
so she climbed over the city wall to enter.
Chē then cut off her feet.
Zhào Chénghóu considered him uncompassionate,
took away his seal, and dismissed him from his post as magistrate.
Guǎn Zhòng, in shackles,
was traveling from Lǔ to Qí.
On the way, he was hungry and thirsty,
so he passed by a border guard of Qǐwū and begged for food.
The border guard of Qǐwū knelt down and fed him,
with great respect.
The border guard then secretly said to Zhòng:
"If by chance
you reach Qí, do not die, and are employed by Qí,
how will you repay me?"
Zhòng said:
"According to your words,
I will employ the virtuous,
task the capable,
and reward the meritorious.
How could I repay you?"
The border guard resented him.
There are three ways a ruler governs his subjects.
Canon One:〓#
If power is insufficient to transform, then eliminate.
Shī Kuàng's response
and Yàn Zǐ's explanation
both abandon the ease of power
and speak of the difficulty of acting virtuously;
this is like chasing a running beast;
it is not knowing how to eliminate the danger.
That the danger can be eliminated lies
in Zǐ Xià's explanation of the *Spring and Autumn Annals*:
"Those who are good at wielding power nip treachery in the bud."
Therefore, Jì Sūn allowed Zhòng Ní to encounter power,
let alone placing it in the hands of a ruler?
That is why Tài Gōngwàng killed Kuáng Yù,
and a slave should not ride a Jì horse.
Sì Gōng knew this,
so he did not drive a deer.
Xuē Gōng knew this,
so he gambled with the two Luán brothers.
These all knew the reversal of similarity and difference.
Therefore, the way a wise ruler manages his ministers
is explained in raising crows.
Canon Two:〓#
The ruler is the linchpin
of benefits and harms.
There are many archers,
therefore rulers are vulnerable.
Thus, if likes and dislikes are revealed,
then inferiors will take advantage,
and the ruler will be confused.
If words and arguments are unobstructed,
then ministers will be difficult to control,
and the ruler will not be perceptive.
The explanation lies in Shēn Zǐ's words on "Six Cautions"
and Táng Yì's words on archery.
The danger lies in Guó Yáng's request to change the laws
and Xuān Wáng's sigh.
Illuminate this with Jìng Guōshì's presentation of ten earrings
and Xī Shǒu's and
Gān Mào's method of listening through a hole in the wall.
Tángxī Gōng understood tactics,
so he asked about the jade cup;
Zhāo Hóu was skilled in tactics,
so he only listened when alone in bed.
The way of a wise ruler
lies in Shēn Zǐ's advice to decide alone.
Canon Three:〓#
There is a reason
why tactics are not implemented.
If you do not kill the dog,
the wine will turn sour.
The state also has dogs,
and those around the ruler are all shrine rats.
The ruler must not have Yáo's second execution
or Zhuāng Wáng's response to the crown prince,
but all must have Bó Ǎo's decision regarding Cài Ǒ.
Knowing value but lacking ability requires using the method of teaching songs to first measure it.
Wú Qǐ's abandoning of his beloved wife
and Wén Gōng's beheading of Diān Xié were
both against their feelings.
Therefore, one who can make others lance boils
must be one who can endure the pain.
Sayings 1: 〓#
To reward and praise without encouraging,
to punish and denigrate without instilling fear,
if all four are applied without change,
then get rid of them.
Qí Jǐng Gōng of Qí went to Jìn,
attending a feast with Píng Gōng,
with Shī Kuàng attending the gathering.
Jǐng Gōng asked Shī Kuàng about governing, saying,
"Great Teacher, what will you teach me?"
Shī Kuàng said,
"Your lord must be kind to the people."
In the middle of the gathering,
the wine at its height,
preparing to leave,
he again asked Shī Kuàng about governing, saying,
"Great Teacher, what will you teach me?"
He said,
"Your lord must be kind to the people, that is all."
Jǐng Gōng left his residence,
Shī Kuàng saw him off,
and again asked Shī Kuàng about governing.
Shī Kuàng said,
"Your lord must be kind to the people, that is all."
Jǐng Gōng returned,
pondering,
not yet awake,
and understood what Shī Kuàng meant:
Gōngzǐ Wěi and Gōngzǐ Xià,
were Jǐng Gōng's two younger brothers,
who greatly pleased the people of Qí,
their families were wealthy and the people liked them,
competing with the ducal house,
they were a danger to my position.
Now, saying that I should be kind to the people,
is that to make me compete with my two younger brothers for the people?
Therefore, upon returning to the state,
he opened the granaries to distribute grain to the poor,
distributed the surplus wealth of the treasury to the orphans and widows,
the granaries had no stored grain,
the treasury had no surplus wealth,
palace women who were not favored were married off,
those seventy years old received salary rice.
Selling virtue and bestowing favor on the people,
he had already competed with his two younger brothers.
After two years,
the two younger brothers fled,
Gōngzǐ Xià fled to Chǔ,
Gōngzǐ Wěi fled to Jìn.
Jǐng Gōng was strolling with Yàn Zǐ at Shào Hǎi,
ascended the Bǎi Qǐn Terrace and looked back at his state,
saying,
"How beautiful!
Vast and grand!
Majestic and imposing!
Who in later generations will have this?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"It will be the Tián Chéng clan!"
Jǐng Gōng said,
"I have this state,
and you say the Tián Chéng clan will have it,
why is that?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"The Tián Chéng clan greatly pleases the people of Qí.
Regarding their treatment of the people,
the requests for ranks and salaries are carried out through the great ministers,
below, they privately use large dòu and hú measures, and qū and fǔ containers
to lend out grain,
and small dòu and hú measures, and qū and fǔ containers to collect it.
Killing one ox,
they take one dòu of meat,
and use the remainder to feed the gentlemen.
Throughout the year,
the cloth and silk are taken in two batches,
and the remainder is used to clothe the gentlemen.
Therefore, the price of timber in the market
is no more expensive than in the mountains;
the fish, salt, turtles, soft-shelled turtles, snails, and clams of the marshes
are no more expensive than in the sea.
Your lord levies heavily,
while the Tián Chéng clan bestows generously.
Qí once experienced a great famine,
the number of those starving to death by the roadside was countless,
fathers and sons pulling each other and rushing to the Tián Chéng clan,
I have not heard of anyone not being saved.
Therefore, the people of Qín and Zhōu sang together, saying,
"Oh,
let it be!
Abundant,
let us go and return to Tián Chéngzǐ!'"
The *Shī* says,
"Although they have no virtue to give you,
we sing and dance."
